scope: Coverage-guided fuzzing must exercise parsers, storage log replay, userspace image metadata, sync frames, capability messages, and kernel/user ABI decoding before release.
current_evidence: Adversarial spec tests reject malformed manifests, corrupted storage logs, stale metadata, and bypass attempts.

The release-security checker runs deterministic mutation fuzzing from checked seed corpora against binary cursors, ELF image metadata, storage volume loading, sync record decoding, capability messages, and syscall ABI range validation, and release-security-check now runs exact-catalog tests proving bundle-controlled trust files and verification workloads cannot enter a production release.
graduation_criteria: Keep release-running fuzz harnesses, checked seed corpora, deterministic mutation counts, crash redaction fixtures, and regression tests wired into release-security-check before tagging.
cisa_alignment: Treat exploit-prone input handling as a manufacturer-owned defect class and block release when parser fuzz evidence is absent.

scope: Fault injection must cover boot artifact tamper, rollback failure, service startup, permission review, power loss, torn writes, storage driver crash/rebind, recovery repair, and sync transport disruption.
current_evidence: QEMU smoke paths include service startup, permission review, tampered artifacts, rollback-slot failure, recovery proof, storage durability, sync two-node, and driver restart gates.
Recovery entry now rejects duplicate action lists and zero boot ticks, while break-glass recovery requires bounded single-line audit reasons before recording approval.

The release-security-preflight target aggregates native smoke tamper profiles, storage durability, driver restart, recovery, sync two-node, TPM transport/sealing/ownership/quotes, both UEFI QEMU paths, and unified-image firmware authentication/tamper rejection before candidate generation; the final verify-only release-security-gate seals the frozen candidate with the real RNUC15CRSU7 proof.
graduation_criteria: Keep service startup, permission review, storage, driver, recovery, sync, boot tamper, rollback, UEFI fault campaigns, and the RNUC15CRSU7 real-hardware proof bundle in the release matrix with deterministic artifacts and failure triage records.
cisa_alignment: Exercise secure-by-default behavior under failure instead of depending on customer recovery workarounds.

scope: Release artifacts must be buildable from pinned inputs with deterministic outputs or documented, bounded nondeterminism.
current_evidence: The repository pins the Zig toolchain entrypoint and keeps generated artifacts under build outputs.

EFI boot media uses a fixed FAT volume identity and UTC timestamps derived from a bounded SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, with a deterministic 1980 default and all media dates clamped to 1980 for earlier epochs. ISO file and volume timestamps and ownership are normalized as well, so filesystem and image metadata do not encode the build clock, host timezone, or host ownership.

The published production kernel and embedded EFI payload use the same debug-stripped ELF with static symbols retained for role checks. The role-gated full diagnostic ELF remains under zig-out/kernel-debug for source-line and type information, outside the 17-target release catalog. Optimized EFI images explicitly omit COFF/PDB debugging metadata, keeping build paths and diagnostic timestamps out of the shipped firmware image.

The reproducible-build-check target exports regular-file contents and executable bits from one immutable Jujutsu revision into two isolated workspaces and checks snapshot stability before building. Each tree uses separate local and global caches to build the exact 17-target production catalog independently with ReleaseFast, the signed evidence label for Zig 0.17 fast mode. It compares the ISO, kernel, seven policy manifests, and 8 userspace-image digests, and records repo_vcs=jj, repository, Jujutsu change ID, commit ID, dirty workspace count, toolchain, optimize mode, and result metadata under build/release-security. EFI media timestamps are explicit build inputs, so SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH changes invalidate cached media. The independently distributed host verifier is outside the OS target catalog.
graduation_criteria: Keep a reproducible-build release target that builds one frozen Jujutsu revision in two isolated workspaces, compares artifact digests, records repository, Jujutsu source identity, toolchain, and environment metadata, and fails on undocumented nondeterminism.
cisa_alignment: Support supply-chain transparency and reduce unverified build inputs before customer distribution.

scope: Every release artifact must carry machine-readable SBOM data, source provenance, signer identity, measured boot inputs, customer-verifiable digest records, and DSSE-wrapped attestations signed by hardware-backed release keys.
current_evidence: Userspace archives, boot measurements, signed bundle state, and launch provenance are modeled and tested.

The release-sbom-provenance and reproducible-build targets emit the exact ten-file evidence catalog for the exact 17-target production catalog; the finalizer privately candidate-verifies before atomically publishing release-manifest.dsse.json as the sole signed digest authority, then performs full stateful verification and withdraws the marker on failure. The vulnerability disclosure dry run stays outside the exact bundle under build/release-audit.

Public generation requires an absolute out-of-band root metadata file and independently supplied lowercase SHA-256 pin, a root-threshold-signed release-trust-policy.dsse.json, an independently distributed verifier with an external SHA-256 pin, an external hardware-backed signing command, and a derived release key id. Static preview signatures, self-authenticating bundled verifiers, and bundle-selected keyrings are not accepted.

The zigos-verify-release customer CLI verifies the root pin, root threshold and release-manifest signatures before parsing their payloads; applies root minimumPolicyVersion and policy minimumReleaseSequence first-use floors; enforces the exact target and evidence sets; applies policy-authenticated revocations and expiry; validates signed SLSA source identity, ReleaseFast mode, measurements, SPDX version, and reproducibility; and serializes persistent rollback/equivocation state outside the bundle and artifact root.

The release-security checker derives all production target and evidence expectations from src/tools/release_catalog.zig, requires the authenticated trust interfaces, and rejects missing, duplicate, unexpected, unsafe, verification-only, or legacy trust artifacts. Candidate inputs remain private and quiescent through verification. Root rotation is deliberately manual: a changed root requires an explicit out-of-band re-pin and state migration.
graduation_criteria: Generate SPDX SBOMs plus DSSE-wrapped in-toto/SLSA provenance attestations for the production kernel, 8 userspace images, policy manifests, and ISO.

Sign each DSSE PAE payload with a hardware-backed TPM, secure enclave, HSM, or KMS release key, publish a root-threshold-signed trust policy and release-key-signed exact manifest, and fail release if the external trust root, independently pinned verifier, signer, sequence, or expiry is absent or invalid.

Keep zigos-verify-release validating the out-of-band root pin, first-use minimumPolicyVersion and minimumReleaseSequence checkpoints, threshold policy signature, release-manifest signature before parsing, exact 17 targets and ten evidence files, signed SLSA identity, zero dirty workspace evidence, revocation and validity, reproducibility, persistent rollback/equivocation state, post-quantum policy, and required ML-DSA coverage for every public release.
cisa_alignment: Maintain SBOMs and transparent vulnerability/exploitability records for first- and third-party software.

scope: Threat-model tests must cover explicit authority, privilege boundaries, boot trust, recovery, policy mediation, storage integrity, sync trust, diagnostics privacy, and driver isolation.
current_evidence: Spec conformance and adversarial tests already encode revoked capability, expired lease, malformed manifest, corrupted log, rollback, bypass, hidden observability, and unsupported continuous process-observation threats.

The kernel capability table now stores live capabilities and target revocation generations in indexed arenas with holder and target multimap indexes, so authority lookup, grant rollback, pass/revoke, holder/target queries, and target-generation reservation no longer depend on bespoke fixed-slot free-list scans.

spec/release_security/threat_model.json publishes a reviewer-facing matrix with threat IDs, abuse cases, mitigations, negative tests, residual-risk owners, and release decisions for every required security domain.
graduation_criteria: Keep the threat-model matrix release-gated and require every P0/P1 release track to list abuse cases, mitigations, negative tests, and residual-risk decisions.
cisa_alignment: Make security properties measurable across the product lifecycle and prevent dangerous defaults from shipping silently.

scope: Unsafe Zig and kernel-adjacent sections must be inventoried, reviewed, minimized, and bound by tests before release, especially pointer casts, integer-pointer conversion, inline assembly, packed ABI structs, and user memory copies.
current_evidence: The kernel and native syscall paths centralize many low-level boundaries and have targeted negative tests around user memory and brokered devices.

Interrupt nesting now uses a cache-line-isolated volatile counter for each bounded logical CPU. Private object-page write faults promote only owned nonexecutable 4 KiB leaves without recopying task changes; read-only zero mappings and reserved-bit, NX, protection-key and shadow-stack faults remain denied. Huge-page allocation requests physically aligned 512-frame runs, validates the 2 MiB physical base before encoding, and falls back to 4 KiB pages under fragmentation. Range retirement clears PRESENT on every validated leaf, invalidates once, and frees private frames only after remote acknowledgement; shootdown timeout stops before reuse. Host regressions cover interleaved CPU nesting, snapshot retention, forbidden fault reasons, aligned allocation in fragmented space, mixed 4 KiB/2 MiB/borrowed leaves, invalid-range atomicity and one invalidation before every frame release. Guest integration still requires XSAVES-capable emulation or hardware.

Shared fixed and paged handle arenas retire physical slots at generation exhaustion without growing metadata or wrapping stale handles into authority. Reset and index rebuild preserve exhausted generations within the arena lifetime; endpoint reset retains generation history while releasing queues and ownership indexes. Replacement at the final live generation fails without mutation. Capability batch grants, shared-memory frame admission, paired vault leases, revoked delegations and closed overlay sessions skip exhausted slots or fail before publishing authority. Snapshot restore preflights destination generations before retiring tasks or changing grants, retaining stable cold slots for surviving tasks and skipping exhausted slots for new tasks. Targeted Debug regressions cover the final live generation, reset, explicit slot reservations, rebuild rejection, full exhaustion and unchanged state after rejected replacements. Handle wire sizes and resident memory ceilings remain unchanged.

spec/release_security/memory_safety_inventory.json inventories every tracked Zig source file containing pointer conversion, pointer casts, inline assembly, packed or extern ABI structs, volatile access, or atomic primitives, and the release-security checker rejects any new unsafe source path without release-reviewed owner, mitigation, and test coverage.
graduation_criteria: Keep an unsafe-surface inventory, required audit owner, reviewer checklist, and tests for every user-memory copy, pointer conversion, inline assembly block, and kernel allocator invariant.
cisa_alignment: Treat memory-safety roadmaps and migration/mitigation evidence as mandatory for unsafe or kernel-adjacent code.

scope: Crash dumps, event-ledger exports, remote diagnostics, and support bundles must redact secrets, private object names, personal content, capability tokens, and raw memory by default.
current_evidence: Event-ledger, supervisor, and spec tests verify redacted diagnostics for crashes, permission decisions, remote shares, and autonomous agent authorization/action denials.

Event-ledger text export writes its common diagnostic fields and decimal identifiers directly into the caller-provided buffer, preserving the stable redacted wire format while reducing the gated export benchmark by roughly 3 to 7 percent.

Steady-state event-ledger rollover resolves the oldest retained slot directly through its maintained order index, avoiding a 64-record scan on every append after capacity; full scans remain limited to state reconstruction and non-contiguous recovery.

Crash record summaries now redact sensitive reason text by default, and spec/release_security/crash_dump_redaction.json gates raw memory denial, opt-in scoped diagnostics, support-bundle review, and reproducible redaction fixtures.

The secret vault stores sealed records in 16 reusable generation-checked slots and leases in a generational arena, with bounded active-at-tick scans. Lookup validates the full key ID in constant time; retirement erases the live record and all leases, and exhausted slot generations never wrap. Hardware-backed imports require an explicit provider; immutable operation tables always pair sealing and opening. A dedicated generation operation checks current vault policy, keeps each fresh Ed25519 seed inside the TPM adapter, erases it on every exit, and returns only a nonexportable sealed record. Missing generation support, entropy failures, malformed provider output, and full tables fail without publication; audit persistence failure rolls back the unpublished record. Imports and rotations now share an erasing rollback path that restores pristine or retired slot IDs without copying the vault. Replacement validation, provider and audit failures leave old leases and unrelated keys unchanged. Lending previews both generation-checked arenas before auditing the exact lease ID, so failed audits consume neither capacity nor generations, including free-list reuse and replacement of revoked or expired leases. Single-handle and whole-secret revocation apply only after audit acceptance. Export buffers are cleared and signatures withheld on audit errors. Regression tests reproduce each mutation-before-error path, repeat failed operations beyond table capacity, and verify successful retries. An unused service rotation counter and its per-handle copy are removed; lease identity remains in arena generations. These serialized in-process guarantees do not replace durable vault checkpoints or production audit retention. TPM cold/reboot verification generates the persisted key through the vault, verifies its public key after restore, and checks distinct keys for repeated owner/label requests. A signed vault catalog durably checkpoints up to 16 sealed records, preserves live key IDs, retired slot generations, owner and export policy, and restores atomically without leases. Its bounded caller-owned buffer supports multi-page snapshots. Explicit failed-barrier retries reuse the pending version; malformed framing, wrong pins, mismatched owners, stale signed generations and failed unseals leave the destination empty. The TPM reboot proof restores three generated keys and a 96-byte exportable secret through the primary catalog, plus the remote catalog signer and current device key through a second catalog, before lending fresh handles. Two remote rotations retire the predecessor records and reuse a slot under a new ID; reboot rejects both retired IDs. Catalog pins, the root pin, generation and exact payload digest now live in separate 136-byte authenticated TPM NV records. NV reads and full-record writes use salted encrypted HMAC sessions with caller authorization; public-area validation rejects weaker access policies. Explicit provisioning refuses existing indexes, and restore never provisions a missing index. The catalog checkpoint waits for disk durability before advancing an attached anchor and retains its pending version on failure. Reboot verification corrupts a successful NV-write response, withholds the assertion, then uses a fresh client to reconcile the exact stored record without rewriting NV. Rolling the native disk back while preserving newer TPM state rejects restore before publishing secrets. Catalog v5 adds a signed predecessor digest; recovery authenticates exactly one successor of the independently pinned generation and digest, confirms disk durability, and completes the NV update before restoring secrets. No extra NV write or larger TPM record is required, and checkpoint coordination remains 112 bytes. Host regressions reject signed forks, skipped generations, unpinned trust and forged signatures, and prove unsigned object-store version links carry no recovery authority. The QEMU guest halts after the disk commit and before sending NV_Write; restarting the VM and TPM completes that checkpoint and resumes the persisted credential counter. Identity recovery runs before unrelated verification journeys mutate storage. This is ordinary authenticated NV with serialized software generation checks, not a hardware monotonic counter. First enrollment now validates and durably commits the complete candidate before defining an immutable domain-separated SHA-256 commitment to the initial anchor and index in the NV authPolicy field; AUTHREAD/AUTHWRITE remain the only data-access methods. Bounded inspection reconstructs an untrusted candidate without unsealing keys or publishing state. Recovery authenticates the committed Name in an HMAC operation, checks WRITTEN using the same public-area snapshot used for first-write authorization, and refuses to redefine missing indexes or overwrite initialized records. Exact completed retries read and compare without another NV write. Host tests cover candidate framing, binding changes, first-write guards and durability failures. QEMU halts between index definition and first write, restarts the VM and TPM, rejects a changed commitment, reconciles a lost successful first-write reply without rewriting, and rejects a forged unwritten status before restore. A bounded PIN capsule now seals random vault authorization under an owner/device/salt-bound PIN authorization, stores no software PIN verifier, requires an independent enrollment digest, checks the enrolled TPM parent Name before sending PIN authorization, and erases failed outputs. Explicit lockout-authority enrollment and rotation encrypt the new value and authenticate the response under it. Dictionary-attack configuration refuses zero recovery intervals and excessive attempt limits; the default is eight attempts, one recovered attempt per powered hour, and a separate 24-hour lockout-administrator retry interval. PIN retries never clear counters. The QEMU proof commits a capsule, changes and rotates lockout authorization (including an accepted change with a damaged reply), exhausts three permitted test guesses, halts, restarts the VM and TPM, observes persistent lockout even for the correct PIN, and releases the same sealed key only after explicit administrator recovery. Host regressions reject untrusted or malformed capsules, invalid PINs, altered owner/device/salt bindings, and disabled guessing limits before hardware access. Independent recovery-material custody, physical TPM persistence evidence, biometric verification and userspace request dispatch remain open.

The OS identity store keeps dense credential metadata and binds non-exportable hardware-backed keys through private service-owned vault leases instead of caller-supplied seeds. Registration derives the public key through authorized signing; assertions recheck vault and credential policy and sign counters plus security claims. Recovery uses the registered approval threshold and binds approvals to the replacement key and current generation. Malformed unlock lengths and ambiguous origins are rejected before signing. Vault catalog format v5 checkpoints up to 16 credentials with their sealed keys, including assertion counters, recovery generations, relying parties and revocations, and rejects older formats. The bounded credential codec validates canonical framing and sealed-key custody, derives redundant security flags and digests, and rolls back the entire key and credential restore on an invalid binding. A durable identity service checkpoints registration, assertion, recovery and revocation before returning success; assertion signatures remain private until their counters reach disk. Failed signing or storage barriers block subsequent identity mutations until an explicit flush succeeds, with retries reusing the pending version. Host crash tests cover withheld assertions, retry, durable revocation, replacement-key recovery, multi-record validation and malformed snapshots. The virtual TPM reboot proof restores credential state, advances the persisted assertion counter and rejects a previously revoked credential. Unlock signatures bind a public boot ID and a fresh service-owned session nonce; lock, verifier restart and entropy failure invalidate old proofs. The fixed 64-byte Ed25519 signature uses the enrolled device public key instead of duplicating it in the request, preserving existing memory ceilings. A trusted authenticator can issue proofs using a private sealed device-key lease; software-seed issuance is restricted to verification builds. Host tests reject stale recovery approvals and signed-context transplantation, and the virtual TPM reboot replays a saved proof at matching relative ticks and rejects it without advancing the credential counter. Independent recovery-material custody, biometric verification and physical TPM validation remain open. One-use native credential grants now bind an exact userspace process and approved RP/origin to its current sign-in session. Applications send only a challenge over authenticated endpoints; four bounded channels share the guarded worker, checkpoint before reply, and cancel on lock, expiry, revocation or process restart. The SDK assembles complete canonical assertions for independent relying-party signature verification. Ownership reboot exercises real Ring3 delivery, a durable counter and cancellation during TPM work. A native consent screen displays the launch-authenticated application ID and full RP/origin, defaults to Cancel, and accepts Allow once only after complete successful scanout and separate released HID gestures. No endpoint exists before consent; approval consumption rechecks the exact process generation, owner, session and original deadline. Lock, timeout, interruption, revocation and process replacement cancel pending requests without TPM work. Host regressions cover display bounds, hostile text, stale authority and gesture isolation; ownership reboot exercises default rejection and explicit HID approval before Ring3 delivery. Signed app provenance is not website authority: authenticated-origin acquisition and credential registration/recovery IPC remain open. An attached TPM NV anchor now withholds assertions until their catalog digest and generation persist independently of disk; failed anchor commits block mutations and retry the same catalog version.
graduation_criteria: Keep explicit crash dump policy tests for raw memory capture denial, opt-in scoped diagnostics, capability token scrubbing, private object-name scrubbing, and reproducible redaction fixtures.
cisa_alignment: Keep security-sensitive telemetry safe by default and avoid shifting diagnostic privacy risk to customers.

scope: A release must have a published vulnerability disclosure policy, private intake channel, triage SLA, CVE/CWE handling process, coordinated disclosure rules, and security update commitments.
current_evidence: SECURITY.md publishes GitHub private vulnerability reporting and a backup security mailbox, with monitored release-security-review ownership, 3-business-day acknowledgement, 10-business-day triage, coordinated disclosure, CVE/CWE handling, and security update commitments.
spec/release_security/vulnerability_disclosure.json encodes the private intake channels, owner, SLA, CVE/CWE process, and dry-run workflow artifact required by the release gate.
graduation_criteria: Keep the private intake channel published, maintainers on rotation, CVE issuance ownership documented, and end-to-end disclosure dry-run recorded before release.
cisa_alignment: Avoid the CISA bad practice of shipping without a scoped vulnerability disclosure policy and timely CVE/CWE process.

first_hardware_target.selection_reason: Single commodity x86_64 UEFI target with ACPI, integrated display output, USB xHCI input path, M.2 NVMe storage, and wired Intel I225-LM Ethernet so the first hardware proof does not depend on Wi-Fi or dongles.
first_hardware_target.boot_medium: Two unified EFI ISO or USB boots: build/os.iso for the shipped production kernel and build/os-verification.iso for the exhaustive verification workload.
first_hardware_target.serial_capture: Separate real-machine production-serial.log and verification-serial.log single-boot captures, plus individually hashed cycles/*.log files, archived under one fresh build/hardware-proofs/<fresh-name>/ ceremony directory as an authenticated proof bundle and checked by scripts/check-nuc15crsu7-hardware-proof.sh.
proof_bundle_requirements: proof-manifest.txt must use the v2 format and tie the bundle to a fresh externally issued 64-hex capture nonce, stable target/device identity, production-serial.log bound to build/os.iso and zig-out/bin/kernel-zigos-native.elf, verification-serial.log bound to build/os-verification.iso and zig-out/bin/kernel-zigos-native-verification.elf, the canonical cycle manifest, both checked marker contracts, both role-specific quote/signature pairs, all checked sidecars, repo_vcs=jj, the current Jujutsu change and commit IDs, repo_dirty_files=0, capture times, and operator.

production-serial.log must be exactly one shipped production-image boot with BOOT:ROLE:production and native-ready, exclude verification-only journeys and cycle summaries, and contain exactly one structured final checkpoint with enabled=true, dirty=false, numeric generation, error=none, and measured-root-before-checkpoint-before-task-ready-before-native-ready ordering.

verification-serial.log must be exactly one verification-image boot with BOOT:ROLE:verification and ZIGOS:NATIVE:READY, real-hardware source and board metadata, every active verification marker, and observation-before-PASS ordering; repeated boot/device/power cycles must not be concatenated into this log.

device-identity.txt, proof-manifest.txt, firmware-settings.txt, power-cycle-notes.txt, and attestation-lifecycle.txt must not contain duplicate required keys, and the stable device ID must match across the manifest, identity, cycles, quotes, and verifier assertion.

firmware-settings.txt must record BIOS/UEFI version, boot_mode=UEFI, secure_boot=enabled and a firmware-authenticated unified image, storage_mode=nvme, wake/suspend settings, and any changed firmware options.

cycle-manifest.txt must canonically index individually hashed, nonce/target/device/type/index-bound cycle logs with unique paths and digests, fixed type order, and contiguous indices; only valid unique entries establish the minimum counts, while power-cycle-notes.txt and verification-serial.log counters are matching summaries.

attestation-lifecycle.txt must record the real-hardware provider, root key id, positive initial generation, higher active generation, positive revoked generation count, stale-generation rejection, revoked-generation rejection, stale-attestation verifier rejection, request-bound verifier metadata digest, 64-hex verifier metadata digest, 64-hex attestation request digest, operator, notes, and captured_at_utc not before the proof manifest prepared_at_utc.

artifact-digests.sha256 must contain only well-formed SHA-256 digest rows and record exactly one SHA-256 digest for both production ISO/kernel artifacts, both verification ISO/kernel artifacts, each hardware marker contract, every required userspace service image, release policy artifact, production readiness manifest, release artifact manifest, and driver image artifact under the checked artifact root.

capture-statement.txt must canonically bind the fresh nonce, stable identity, repo IDs, both single-boot log hashes, cycle-manifest hash, both ISO/kernel pairs, both marker contracts, every sidecar, and separate production/verification quote and signature hashes; the checker independently recomputes every hash.

Normal checking must fail without ZIGOS_HARDWARE_PROOF_EXPECTED_NONCE, an absolute external ZIGOS_HARDWARE_PROOF_VERIFIER, and an externally pinned ZIGOS_HARDWARE_PROOF_VERIFIER_SHA256 matching that executable; exit status alone is insufficient and verifier output must exactly assert signed-response, statement digest, nonce, target/device identity, and both verified roles.
hardware_exit_criteria: A separate shipped production ISO boot reaches native-ready on the RNUC15CRSU7 with BOOT:ROLE:production, target identity and early ACPI evidence, essential service and measured-boot readiness, and a clean final checkpoint without verification-only markers, panic, hang, or firmware fallback.

At least ten individually hashed cold-boot logs and ten individually hashed warm-reboot logs reach the required result on the same nonce-bound RNUC15CRSU7 identity without panic, hang, or firmware fallback.

ACPI table discovery, APIC timer interrupt proof, GOP framebuffer scanout proof, USB xHCI keyboard input, NVMe read/write, Intel I225-LM transmit/receive, suspend/resume, crash persistence, and update rollback each emit the required hardware target marker plus the corresponding concrete fact marker from the verification workload.

Generated userspace startup, service IPC connectivity, compositor framebuffer presentation, permission review rendering, sync replication/restart, driver restart/rebind, crash-record persistence, and update rollback health checks emit the required booted verification-workload markers.
Twenty suspend/resume cycles preserve timer, framebuffer, USB input, NVMe, and network usability.

Ten induced crash-recovery cycles preserve the native store and produce redacted recovery diagnostics, and ten crash-record persistence checks prove those diagnostics survive reboot without exposing raw memory.
Ten update rollback cycles survive real power transitions and return to the verified active slot without losing persisted state.

Every hardware proof bundle includes separate production and verification single-boot output, individually hashed cycle logs, a canonical statement binding all artifacts/contracts/sidecars and two role quotes/signatures, plus an exact assertion from an external verifier whose executable digest and fresh nonce are pinned outside the bundle.
open_gaps: Neither required RNUC15CRSU7 production nor verification serial log has been captured from real hardware yet.

The kernel preserves the native EFI handoff in a tagged Multiboot2-compatible layout, validates memory-map, GOP framebuffer, and ACPI RSDP descriptors, scans only SMBIOS 3+ entry points for the RNUC15CRSU7 SKU, and composes mapped ACPI MADT/FADT/MCFG and APIC evidence, but those paths have not been captured from the selected NUC firmware.

A shipped production-image boot still needs capture for early target and clean native-ready evidence; real-device xHCI keyboard input reports, NVMe read/write cycles, Intel I225-LM transmit/receive cycles, compositor framebuffer presentation, suspend/resume loops, induced crash-recovery loops, persisted crash-record checks, update rollback power-cycle loops, and booted verification-workload markers still need execution and capture from the verification image.

tracks.title: Object store and storage volume durability
current_evidence: Content-addressed objects use signed metadata, chunked blob records, and Merkle-addressed payload manifests.

Workspace transactions reject zero object or version identities, preflight tombstones and capacity before publication, apply deletions before additions, and publish staged mutation records in place. Snapshot replay applies complete generation batches with the same ordering; full-table updates retain existing paths. Restore records against stable entries and copies its prepared target once instead of shifting the live array per mutation. Generation advancement stops before the reserved all-ones snapshot sentinel. Focused regressions cover full-capacity replacement, replay/export, staged revival overflow, invalid-deletion atomicity and generation exhaustion. Matched Zig 0.17 fast host measurements of signed-package restore over 64 entries with 64 original mutation records retained and 128 restore deltas reduced the five-sample median from 85559.10 to 78966.03 ns with checksum 333709050; signing setup and result validation were outside timing, while signature verification remained inside.
The storage volume can save and replay segmented logs through image-backed and attached-volume paths, with generic test callbacks isolated from target NVMe PCI attachments by distinct backend kinds.

Compacted storage checkpoints serialize directly into the bounded inactive log region, reserving and finalizing the record header in place instead of retaining a second payload-sized staging buffer; exact-fit and one-byte-short regressions cover header, length, checksum, and overflow behavior. Paired ReleaseFast builds reduce production writable load by 393,216 bytes (13,437,124 to 13,043,908) and verification writable load by 389,120 bytes (21,760,196 to 21,371,076), while paired default builds reduce them by 782,336 and 786,432 bytes respectively.

Freestanding storage activation now requires brokered device publication or an attached, capacity-checked NVMe bridge and fails closed when neither exists instead of synthesizing an ephemeral RAM disk; hosted model builds retain their in-memory test backend, while paired default `verify` builds reduce production writable load by 794,624 bytes (15,988,736 to 15,194,112) and increase headroom from 788,480 to 1,583,104 bytes with `.data` unchanged at 10,202,800 bytes.

Host tests cover corrupted payload rejection, malformed root-log metadata, torn-record rejection, compaction, page-sized payload reload, undersized image rejection without state mutation, power-loss before root commit, partial-sector log corruption fallback, long-running replay/compaction gates, indexed workspace/snapshot replay, production storage attachment-kind separation, and shared-memory transfer into the storage service.

Workspace share grants now keep a resident principal index rebuilt with workspace state, workspace path indexes maintain object-id slots, workspace and snapshot arenas expose resident counts and indexed snapshot-id lookup, workspaces cache the oldest live snapshot generation for mutation-log compaction guards, and the object store tracks the latest inserted version id, max blob payload bytes, and object-type buckets, so object access, any-access, reshare policy checks, object-to-path share resolution, latest-version retrieval, type-scoped object queries, snapshot existence checks, dirty-snapshot persistence, compaction safety checks, and quota payload usage use keyed or cached lookups instead of scanning storage tables.

Bounded object queries now scan the complete matching arena or type-index chain into a caller-backed worst-root heap, selecting the global newest k results in O(n log k) time with deterministic object-id tie ordering; rejected candidates do not copy their fixed metadata buffers, and regressions cover non-monotonic timestamps, equal-timestamp ties, filters, and rebuilt indexes.

Workspace transactions scrub exactly the live staged-entry prefix on commit or abort, and replacement-only commits update touched Merkle leaves, fold the cached root once, and rebuild object-id slots only when identity changes; structural changes retain full index normalization and inactive-digest scrubbing. An identical 128-commit benchmark alternating same-object and changed-object replacements measured 365,914.06-366,070.31 cycles per operation with unconditional rebuilds versus 201,023.43-211,265.62 incrementally, a 42.3-45.1 percent reduction with identical checksums. Three consecutive post-timer KVM samples measure 5,794.63-6,592.62 cycles per operation with checksum 8,077,187,968,422,010,855; the checked-in baseline uses the slowest sample with a 50 percent regression allowance and a 12,000-cycle hard ceiling.

Read-only file-bridge projections now borrow the directory-owned workspace entry only for immediate metadata extraction instead of copying its fixed path buffer through the resolver callback. The public value-returning workspace API remains available for callers that need an owned snapshot, while the borrow is explicitly invalidated by directory mutation. Two checksum-matched QEMU samples measure 2,051.22-2,053.40 cycles per resolve versus 2,369.75 on paired main, a 13.4 percent reduction, and the hard ceiling is tightened from 3,000 to 2,300 cycles per operation.
The first supported storage envelope is exported from storage_volume.first_supported_capacity_envelope and checked before image or attached-volume persistence.

Writes that exceed the first supported envelope have an explicit user-facing quota policy: reject without partial persistence, report storage.quota.* limit codes, surface NoSpaceLeft at the persistence gate, and reject undersized demo images instead of carrying migration paths; attached-volume production persistence and native-store root adoption require a capacity-checked NVMe PCI backend rather than a generic callback backend.

The storage durability QEMU target reuses one native store image across forced reboots, interrupted writes, and one bad root slot, while benchmark thresholds now gate segmented replay and forced checkpoint compaction. It acknowledges a document save only after an explicit durable checkpoint and verifies the saved payload after cold reboot.

Explicit document saves require an attached device and a complete transaction boundary, checkpoint object bytes and their workspace pointer together, return a nonzero checkpoint generation only after persistence succeeds, reuse an unacknowledged version across retries, and reject stale editor versions. Host fault tests separate volatile device writes from successful flushes and prove failed saves are not acknowledged, interrupted data disappears after power loss, and empty documents remain valid.

The default chunk pool now matches the 640-blob quota so distinct small document and service payloads do not exhaust a separate 224-slot pool first. Compact 16-bit chunk references cover the quota, and freestanding payload bytes still allocate on demand. Blob publication reserves metadata before allocating chunks, unwinds newly allocated chunks on failure, and delays object and version publication until payload allocation succeeds. Host tests fill the complete blob quota, reject overflow without changing storage, reload all payloads from a durable image, and repeat partial multi-chunk allocation failures before retrying successfully. This remains a finite quota; automatic version-history reclamation is not implemented.

Diagnostic ledger format v4 writes one immutable format header and derives its next sequence from the newest retained event on reload, eliminating the extra header version and blob formerly created on every append. Older header layouts are rejected. Bulk imports also batch workspace commits within the staging limit, reserving room for expired paths and replacements. Tests import two complete boot histories within the existing storage envelope, retain the newest events on reload, and respect caller-owned persistence deferral.
capacity_envelope: Volume image: 786432 bytes across 1536 required device sectors, with 785408 bytes available for replay logs.
Object store: 192 objects, 768 versions, 640 blobs, 640 chunks, 28 chunks per payload, 4096-byte chunks, and a 114688-byte maximum object payload.
Workspace state: 8 workspaces, 96 entries per workspace, and 16 snapshots.
Replay gate: 512 log records and 64 segment boundaries before compaction must write a new checkpoint.
Over-limit write behavior: no truncation, eviction, implicit expansion, or partial persistence; callers must free space or move to a larger product envelope before retrying.

Keep disk-chaos QEMU tests that write, reboot, interrupt, corrupt one slot, compact, and prove deterministic recovery.
Keep benchmark thresholds for storage replay, checkpoint compaction, workspace commit, file-bridge read, and memory pressure at target data sizes.

tracks.title: Boot, attestation, and base update trust chain
current_evidence: Native EFI images embed the exact stripped kernel ELF and command line. The loader rejects unsafe ELF layouts, reserves destination pages before copying, allocates the early heap through firmware, and carries SHA-256 payload measurements plus explicit firmware authentication status into the kernel. Runtime measurement snapshots and fixture-signed manifests establish consistency only; unsigned QEMU boots report unverified_boot and cannot produce authenticated runtime measured-state attestations. The kernel loads at 32 MiB to avoid low firmware ACPI NVS/runtime allocations. The frame allocator reserves the exact kernel and separately allocated heap ranges while retaining free gaps. Firmware authentication requires enforcing Secure Boot state. The former serialized bootloader-provided provenance value is rejected rather than upgraded.

TCG2 firmware extends SHA-256 PCR 11 with a versioned kernel/options/authentication descriptor, copies a bounded event-log prefix into reserved memory, and verifies its replay against a firmware TPM read. After CRB initialization the kernel independently replays the copied log and checks the live PCR before emitting BOOT_MEASUREMENT:VERIFIED. Missing protocols remain unmeasured; partial extensions, unsupported SHA-256 banks, truncated logs, malformed algorithm tables and changed PCR values fail rather than upgrading provenance. Host tests cover framing, multiple banks, earlier events, duplicate measurements, altered payloads and copied-log reservations. Disposable TPM cold/reboot and Secure Boot cases exercise the actual firmware and native PCR reads.

The TPM client creates restricted ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 attestation keys under its enrolled storage parent using encrypted salted HMAC sessions. Quote generation requires an independently pinned public identity; verification checks the exact PCR 11 selection, expected digest, qualified signer, nonce and ECDSA signature. Verifier-owned challenges use caller entropy and monotonic time, expire within one minute, reject clock rollback and cannot succeed twice. Cold/reboot QEMU runs recover wrapped keys, exceed transient resource capacity without leaks, and reject stale challenges, wrong authorization, altered enrollment, private-blob corruption and damaged session HMACs. TPM replacement rejects the independently authenticated parent pin. The enrollment authority in that proof remains a verification-only fixture excluded from production kernels.
Runtime measured-state attestation refuses both emulator-rooted and unverified measured state and requires a provisioned non-software root.

A/B base selection, rollback, post-activation health markers, and selector-derived power-cycle rollback proof are covered by host logic, QEMU smoke evidence before native-ready, and required real-hardware proof markers.

The native smoke target now includes negative QEMU runs that reject a tampered boot artifact manifest, direct bootloader-measurement digest mutation, direct kernel/userspace-image/policy/driver-set measurement tampering, and a rollback target whose slot measurement no longer verifies before the boot can reach native-ready.

The signature envelope and signing CLI support Ed25519 and a provider-backed production ML-DSA-65 FIPS 204 profile with full-size signature storage and fail-closed verification for unsupported formats; the former Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 hybrid preview commitment profile has been removed so no placeholder post-quantum path exists in the envelope.

A signature-provider boundary and registry now report provider profile, key custody, hardware-backed release eligibility, lifecycle controls, customer-verifier protocol, FIPS 204/FIPS 140 validation metadata, and fail-closed profile mismatches so production Ed25519 or validated ML-DSA providers can be swapped in without changing manifest storage layouts.

Attestation statements carry verifier-visible nonempty hardware root key ids and nonzero generations, verifier expectations can reject stale or revoked generations after provider rotation, and visible remote attestations now require fresh bounded challenge nonces with bounded replay-cache rejection before signing.

Remote attestation signatures bind a domain-separated context covering the complete verifier request and actual provider metadata, including nonce, remote party, visibility, policy label, origin and key restrictions, minimum generation, revocations, and required metadata. Relabeled requests, rewritten contexts, substituted metadata, and repackaged standalone statements fail verification. Lengths and canonical unused fields are checked before slicing or hashing; signing and provisioning failures leave committed state unchanged. The response stays 616 bytes, and trusted verification performs one signature check.

Attestation roots now have a production external-provider implementation that provisions key-handle metadata for TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or cloud-KMS custody, rejects local-software custody for production roots, requires verifier metadata digests for production providers, and verifies callback signatures against the provisioned public identity before issuing remote-attestation responses.

Production attestation descriptors now reject fake, mock, fixture, smoke, test-only, local-software, synthetic, or simulated operational names before provider metadata or external-provider initialization can treat a root as production eligible.

Platform-service and booted service-path attestation proofs now provision production external-provider key handles instead of test-only fake roots, require verifier metadata digests in the attestation challenge, and pin those digests into downstream network identity policy.

The RNUC15CRSU7 hardware proof model now accepts attestation root lifecycle evidence only from real-target proofs that rotate to a higher root generation, propagate at least one revoked generation, reject stale and revoked root generations, bind the verifier metadata digest to the attestation challenge, and observe verifier rejection of stale attestations; unit tests reject QEMU, stale-rotation, missing-revocation, missing-stale-rejection, and missing-metadata-binding proofs, and the hardware proof bundle checker now requires both the emitted ATTESTATION_ROOT_LIFECYCLE marker and a structured attestation-lifecycle.txt sidecar with generation, revocation, rejection, metadata-digest, and request-digest evidence.

Release-signing and attestation external providers now emit verifier metadata records that own their public key bytes and bind provider name, key id, generation, custody boundary, lifecycle controls, verifier protocol, public key, and FIPS posture into a digest; host tests prove stale, local-software, validation-mismatched, or public-key-tampered metadata fails to match the provider, while public release trust is independently anchored by a pinned root digest and root-threshold-signed policy rather than bundle-controlled key metadata.

Userspace package signatures, boot artifact manifest signatures, generated archive signatures, and attestation statement signatures now route through provider boundaries instead of directly selecting raw Ed25519 operations; the native smoke boot artifact manifest path uses a release-eligible provider fixture so smoke signing exercises key-handle based custody semantics.

Demo seed packages, SDK simulator release bundles, rendered-shell journeys, package-service fixtures, and spec release fixtures now select the Ed25519 provider explicitly where they model release signing behavior.

Package-service update gates now reject exact signed replay, active-version regression, publisher drift, update-channel drift, update-source drift, schema-version regression, empty install sources, oversized install source identities, and invalid data schema versions, including adversarial spec coverage for freshly signed downgrade metadata.

Post-activation health checks now query live healthy and contract-bound supervisor state in constant time instead of depending on bounded diagnostic history; host tests prove readiness survives audit-ring rollover, drops on crash, and returns after restart, and the kernel benchmark gates the lookup cost.

Installed package launch plans, resolved active manifests, and rollback targets now fail closed when the package publisher key has been revoked, so revocation blocks both future updates and already-installed code paths.

The remote TPM attestation service binds the complete verifier request, independently enrolled device/key/generation and approved PCR 11 into quote extraData. Responses contain only bounded TPM evidence; verifier-owned challenges expire within one minute, reject clock rollback and can succeed only once. Native driver and endpoint admission consumes the verified result through egress capabilities and distinct enrollment/PCR-profile pins. Cold/reboot swtpm proofs authorize an encrypted session with actual quotes and reject rewritten policy context, wrong PCR, wrong peer/service, expiry and replay. Failed service calls erase outputs and do not consume the remote nonce. This path does not promote runtime BootRecord provenance or establish EK trust.

TPM peer challenges now bind the full authenticated Noise session. Canonical records fit in at most 402 bytes and three encrypted datagrams; retries reuse ciphertext and nonce values. Locally configured connection preflight blocks object admission until the verifier accepts the quote and the prover receives its encrypted acceptance. The existing four-handle owner allocates optional preflight state only at authorized open, wakes the quote owner once and shares two dispatcher operations among handshake, attestation and object traffic. TPM commands run outside packet dispatch; release, expiry, clock rollback, capability revocation and task retirement reject late completions. Host tests cover lost/reordered/corrupted fragments, malformed authenticated framing, stale handles, duplicate admission during preflight and durable transfer. The cold/reboot swtpm gate exchanges an actual quote between two Noise endpoints in one guest. Operational enrollment, policy provisioning, independent-machine attestation and physical hardware validation remain open.

A trusted native owner can bind a cooperative TPM quote worker to the session scheduler. The worker snapshots locally provisioned credentials, owns its TPM client and guarded stack, and never borrows a connection pointer across a yield. Polling is limited to once per tick; credential expiry/revocation, changed enrollment, service revocation, clock rollback and stale handles cancel publication while retained buffers drain safely. Visibility and nonce history commit only after current policy validation and successful connection delivery. Quote and PIN/recovery workers hold a shared ownership lease through TPM cleanup, allowing queued cancellation without hardware access. Reset and failed boot drain borrowed worker state before releasing services. Host tests cover cancellation, buffer lifetime, queue contention, failure publication and scheduler teardown. Cold/reboot swtpm proofs cancel before Quote and after evidence exists, reject completed delivery, verify stack/snapshot erasure, then retry the same challenge successfully. Operational credential provisioning and independent-machine hardware attestation remain open.

The EFI loader now reconciles the TCG2 final-events table after successful ExitBootServices, retaining firmware mappings until a bounded allocation-free copy finishes. Preexisting mirrored entries must match an exact event-aligned suffix and retain the same count and byte commitment; only new records are appended within the existing 256 KiB budget. Invalid memory extents, duplicate table discovery, changed overlap, malformed counts, truncation and overflow reject boot. Handoff v2 retains its 56-byte layout and rejects the former pre-exit scope. The kernel validates digest-authenticated exit invocation/success and retry ordering, compares PCR 5 replay with the live TPM, and retains the separate PCR 11 loader-image check. Host regressions and firmware QEMU gates cover this path; other PCR verification, physical firmware validation, remote trust policy and PCR-bound secret policies remain open.
production_gaps: Host evidence still uses emulator-provided measurement fallbacks, and external-provider callbacks still route through software fixtures until real hardware or managed-key services are wired.

The provider, request/response, key-handle custody, rotation, revocation, and verifier protocol boundaries exist in source, but the first operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS-backed root has not been provisioned on real hardware.

No local FIPS 204 ML-DSA implementation exists; the production path is the ml-dsa-65 external provider profile with FIPS validation metadata, and Ed25519 remains the only local signing profile until that provider is linked.

Release artifact signing, measurement snapshot, and update rollback now have provider-bound smoke-level tamper rejection, selector-derived power-cycle rollback proof, and QEMU rollback markers, but they are not yet tied to a real TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS deployment or captured on real hardware.

Production unified-image signing and firmware signer enrollment remain unprovisioned. Secure Boot state is local provenance, not a TPM PCR quote, release signer identity, or hardware anti-rollback policy; those bindings and physical-machine captures remain open. Public fixture manifest keys are not production release authorities.

PCR 11 replay and reads establish local measurement consistency only. Nonce-bound quotes now verify the pinned key and expected PCR value, but operational key enrollment, manufacturer/EK certification, release-policy approval of PCR values, deployed verifier policy, enrollment distribution and remote challenge transport remain open. Final events are collected through ExitBootServices and PCR 5 and PCR 11 are compared locally. Physical-firmware validation, verification of the other PCRs and PCR-bound secret policies remain open.
graduation_criteria: Introduce a hardware-root abstraction that supports TPM and secure enclave backed quote/sign operations without exposing root seed material.
Add verifier-facing attestation request and response records with nonce, remote party, policy visibility, key rotation, and revocation tests.

Link an audited FIPS 204 ML-DSA provider through the external provider boundary, bind its validation identity into a future root-signed policy revision, and move rollout from shadow to canary to required after verifier evidence passes.
Broaden release-image tamper gates from smoke fixtures to direct bootloader measurement mutation cases under operational signing keys.
next_actions: Wire the production root provider interface to the first supported TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS implementation and keep fake providers test-only.
Capture the attestation root lifecycle proof in the RNUC15CRSU7 hardware proof bundle after the first operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS root is provisioned.

Move explicit software-provider release fixtures onto operational Ed25519 plus ML-DSA key provisioning once the hardware-backed root, FIPS validation metadata, and release key-management interfaces exist.

Replace the release-eligible smoke signing fixture with the first operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS-backed signing command and publish concrete verifier metadata digests from that provider.
Capture the update rollback marker group in the RNUC15CRSU7 hardware proof bundle.

tracks.title: First real hardware target: Intel RNUC15CRSU7
current_evidence: The first supported hardware target is pinned to Intel NUC 15 Pro Mini PC RNUC15CRSU7 instead of a generic PC-compatible bucket.

The target contract enumerates UEFI boot, ACPI tables, Intel VT-d discovery, hardware-enforced VT-d storage isolation, APIC timer, GOP framebuffer, USB xHCI input, NVMe block I/O, Intel I225-LM network, compositor framebuffer presentation, suspend/resume, crash recovery, crash-record persistence, and update rollback power cycling as required hardware proof.

Early kernel diagnostics are serial-only, while graphical output is owned by the validated UEFI GOP framebuffer and native compositor; the fixed VGA text buffer driver is absent and production readiness rejects its restoration. Supported boots initialize the calibrated invariant-TSC clock before their first marker, COM1 transmit readiness uses a 100 ms elapsed deadline with processor hints, and byte writes no longer wait synchronously for the transmitter to drain; the unsupported-CPU diagnostic path remains bounded and best-effort because no trustworthy clock exists.
The build exposes OVMF-backed uefi-qemu-test and uefi-verification-qemu-test preflights for the production and verification ISO paths before attempting both images on the NUC firmware.

The Multiboot2-only entry path preserves bootloader magic and info pointers, asks GRUB to keep a 32-bit framebuffer payload, and exposes tested tagged memory-map, framebuffer, and ACPI 2 RSDP handoff parsers for runtime proof capture; the obsolete ACPI 1 tag is ignored and production readiness rejects restoration of either that path or the retired Multiboot1 parser.

The Intel VT-d parser validates the current DMAR revision, host address width, firmware opt-out and reserved flags, ordered remapping structures, register-set sizing and alignment, device scopes, reserved-memory regions, and ATS capabilities. The enforcement path rejects non-PCI reserved-memory owners and non-segment-zero units, revokes every discovered PCI bus master, disables INTx, MSI, and MSI-X, requires coherent page walks and x2APIC interrupt-remapping mode, installs shared deny-by-default DMA and interrupt-remapping tables across every remapping unit, assigns NVMe, I225-LM, and xHCI independent requester domains, maps only their direction-scoped queue, buffer, ring, table, scratchpad, and context pages, performs the architected root-pointer, interrupt-table-pointer, and register or queued invalidation handshakes, confirms both translation states on every unit, and only then permits device bus mastering.

The kernel tree now has a tested FADT parser and ACPI suspend/resume proof model for PM control blocks, PM event blocks, SCI wake interrupts, PM timer advancement, reset plumbing, and resumed timer/framebuffer/xHCI/NVMe/I225 subsystem usability, plus a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses the NUC suspend/resume marker unless PM1 sleep writes, S-state entry observations, S0 resume observations, PM timer resume reads, SCI wake interrupts, and post-resume subsystem probes are present.

The kernel tree now has a tested UEFI GOP-style linear framebuffer descriptor validator with stride, buffer-size, pixel-format, and text-grid checks, plus a scanout proof that requires sampled framebuffer bytes to be nonblank and contain an expected rendered pixel, and a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses the NUC GOP framebuffer marker unless GOP mode-info reads, framebuffer base/stride observations, framebuffer memory-read bytes, display scanout observations, expected-pixel observations, captured scanline bytes, and sink-signal observations are present.

The native compositor framebuffer path now has a tested presentation proof with frame dimensions, byte counts, nonblank coverage, a content digest, active-window evidence, visible-window evidence, and expected rendered text before booted compositor markers are emitted.

The kernel tree now has a bounded crash-record format with checksum validation, redacted summary output, and executable persistence proof that validates recovered records across advanced boot ids, plus a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses the NUC crash recovery and persistence markers unless crash-handler entries, persistent record writes and flushes, reboot observations, recovery-boot reads, recovered-record validations, redacted report emissions, and persistent byte counts are present.

Every fixed cache-disabled kernel mapping for NVMe, PCIe ECAM, I225-LM, xHCI capability registers, ACPI root and child tables, and all supported VT-d units now derives from one page-aligned MMIO layout. The layout rejects zero-sized, misaligned, overflowing, or pairwise-overlapping regions at compile time, while each consumer also compile-time checks that its maximum mapping span fits its reserved region, so later PCI configuration access cannot replace a device register page.

PCI discovery now requires a checksum-validated ACPI MCFG segment-zero allocation, computes full 4 KiB PCIe ECAM function addresses, serializes access through one remapped cache-disabled page, and contains no CF8/CFC configuration-port fallback; it walks the reachable hierarchy from bus zero, follows PCI-to-PCI bridge secondary buses, and caches one bounded boot inventory so NVMe, I225-LM, xHCI, graphics, and media queries do not repeat exhaustive 256-bus scans or reserve the full ECAM aperture.

The kernel tree now has a tested NVMe inventory shim with controller-capability parsing, admin-queue validation, fail-closed kernel data-plane transfer behavior, sector-aligned read/write completions, modeled MMIO queue doorbells, page-aligned PRP/DMA evidence, completion-head accounting, deterministic write/read cycle proof generation, and a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses NUC storage markers unless controller-written completions, DMA read/write byte counts, interrupt evidence, and phase-tag observations are present. The real I/O completion queue enables single-message vector-zero interrupts, installs an exact-requester VT-d remapped MSI route on IDT vector 66 after x2APIC initialization, and lets runtime commands idle in HLT with timer-backed deadline wakeups while restoring the caller's interrupt mask after every wake; boot-time administration retains bounded polling. Large reads and writes use two independent 128 KiB bounce/PRP slots, keep two commands outstanding, overlap host copies with device I/O, preserve a separate elapsed deadline for each CID, and accept out-of-order completions only when the CID still belongs to an active slot.

The kernel tree now has a tested Intel I225-LM inventory shim with RX/TX ring-plan validation, descriptor-backed software proof cycles, and a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses NUC packet markers unless hardware-owned TX/RX descriptor evidence, DMA byte counts, asserted interrupts, and PHY packet observations are present. The real target validates BAR0 and the permanent unicast MAC, keeps bus mastering revoked while programming separate 64-entry advanced-descriptor rings, confines both descriptor pages and independent 32-page TX/RX buffer regions in an I225-only direction-scoped VT-d domain, queues transmit descriptors without per-packet completion spinning, reclaims completions in order, applies bounded backpressure without overwriting device-owned slots, timestamps every submission, contains the controller when the oldest descriptor remains incomplete for one second, latches and masks MSI queue causes in the interrupt top half, drains up to eight frames per deferred runtime pass into a fixed 32-frame software queue, wakes the owning network task, rechecks work with interrupts disabled before idle, wraps native payloads in padded local-experimental Ethernet frames, routes service and sync traffic to validated peer unicast MAC addresses, reserves broadcast for scoped discovery, accepts only directed or broadcast frames with that EtherType, recycles receive descriptors after every completion, polls VT-d faults on transmit and receive entry, and disables both queues plus bus mastering on a DMA fault or transmit stall.

The kernel tree now has a tested xHCI input inventory shim with an xHCI 1.1+ baseline, a shared typed PCI memory-BAR decoder, and a dedicated read-only cache-disabled page for live capability-register validation before USB-controller inventory publication. Capability parsing masks the architectural 11-bit interrupter field, requires 64-bit DMA addressing, distinguishes 32- and 64-byte context formats, reconstructs the split 10-bit scratchpad count, and rejects scratchpad restore state when no buffers exist. Its typed DMA arena uses overflow-checked arithmetic and disjoint range validation to reserve a page-contained DCBAA, page-aligned scratchpad pointer and buffer storage, one complete 32-entry Device Context, compact endpoint-zero and interrupt-IN transfer rings, and a cache-line-separated report buffer per enabled slot, plus one shared 64 KiB-aligned writable enumeration buffer and one page-contained reusable 33-entry Input Context after the command and event pages plus ERST. The real halted-controller path allocates and clears the exact contiguous frame run, installs cycle-one self-link TRBs for the command ring and every slot-private control and interrupt ring, initializes the 64-byte primary ERST, DCBAA scratchpad entry and scratchpad pointer array, requires controller support for 4 KiB pages, and programs DCBAAP, CRCR, ERSTSZ, ERSTBA, ERDP, and a 125 microsecond moderation interval with readback validation. It exports six or eight page-granular direction-scoped windows as a third requester domain in the same deny-by-default VT-d transaction as NVMe and I225-LM while bus mastering and interrupts remain disabled; transfer rings are controller-readable while report buffers are controller-write-only. That page is remapped as a bounded sliding window over the extended-capability chain; malformed, overlong, and out-of-range capability states are rejected. When USB legacy support is present, ownership is requested with the architected 8-bit OS-semaphore write, readback must retain OS ownership, and firmware must clear its semaphore within a one-second invariant-TSC deadline. Attach then waits for CNR to clear, clears Run/Stop and interrupt enables, requires HCHalted within the specified 16 ms bound, asserts HCRST, and requires reset completion plus a ready, halted, error-free final state within bounded elapsed deadlines. While the controller remains halted, attach programs CONFIG.MaxSlotsEn to the smaller of the controller capacity and the kernel's 32-slot table, preserves unrelated CONFIG fields, and requires exact readback. The window is restored read-only immediately after every write, and bus mastering remains disabled. No input device is published until keyboard enumeration and hardware event-ring evidence exist. The shim also covers controller-capability parsing, aligned doorbell/runtime offset validation, command/event ring validation, USB boot-keyboard descriptor enumeration, port connection, constant-time device-slot allocation and disconnect reuse, stale-report clearing across hot-plug boundaries, device-slot enable/address, the first device-descriptor control transfer, full-speed endpoint-zero packet-size evaluation, complete device-descriptor retrieval and identity retention, complete first-configuration retrieval and streaming tree validation, alternate-setting-zero boot-keyboard selection, exact Set Configuration completion, exact interface-scoped HID Set Protocol (Boot) completion, real Configure Endpoint context and command completion, configured interrupt-IN endpoint validation, modeled MMIO command and transfer doorbells, device/input/endpoint context-memory ownership evidence, ERST setup evidence, runtime event-ring counters, event-counted input delivery, fail-closed USB input report behavior, and a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses NUC keyboard markers unless hardware event TRBs, event-ring DMA writes, controller context reads, interrupt assertions, port-status changes, and input-report DMA bytes are present.

Deferred xHCI activation now requires the requester-specific VT-d domain, fault monitoring, and interrupt remapping before installing vector 67 MSI and enabling PCI bus mastering. The primary interrupter is enabled before Run/Stop, controller start is bounded by invariant-TSC elapsed time, and the interrupt top half only latches work and acknowledges x2APIC. The native idle loop drains no more than the fixed 64-entry event ring per pass, honors cycle ownership across wrap, advances ERDP to the first unconsumed TRB while clearing EHB, and rechecks the ring before HLT. DMA faults, invalid port-status or transfer events, unsupported event types, ERDP rejection, transfer timeout, and unexpected halt or error states quiesce the controller and revoke MSI plus bus mastering.

After endpoint configuration, the real xHCI path now clears the slot-private report buffer, posts one exact eight-byte Normal TRB on the selected interrupt-IN DCI, validates the hardware Transfer Event against its TRB pointer, slot, DCI, completion code, residual length, and Event Data flag, enqueues the DMA result in a fixed 64-report sequence queue while retaining the latest state, and immediately recycles the next ring entry. Queue capacity reserves space for every controller-owned TD, stops polling instead of dropping reports when full, and rearms unowned endpoints after consumers free space. Reused slots clear and relink both transfer rings before Address Device so stale cycle-owned TRBs cannot execute. Completed reports publish the input-device inventory record and feed a hardware-only input proof assembled from the observed event ring, interrupt, port-change, context, doorbell, and DMA-byte counters; modeled evidence cannot satisfy that path.

The compositor-owned input router now finds task inboxes through an exact resident index and delivers scheduler wake targets through a constant-time intrusive queue; draining, dropping, pruning, and reusing an inbox unlink both structures before slot reuse, preventing stale or duplicate wakes without per-poll inbox scans.

xHCI Supported Protocol ranges may leave architecturally legal port-number gaps but may not overlap; every capability must carry the USB name and a supported 2.0, 3.0, 3.1, or 3.2 revision, while explicit PSI entries define the only accepted speed identifiers and low/full/high-speed class. Deferred port handling preserves PORTSC sticky controls, acknowledges only asserted RW1CS changes, applies normal or warm reset without echoing PED/LWS, and retains an invariant-TSC reset deadline. The DMA arena packs one self-linking 16-TRB endpoint-zero control ring and one interrupt-IN ring per enabled slot, cache-line-separates each report buffer, retains one shared 64 KiB-aligned enumeration buffer, and provides one page-contained reusable Input Context. One serialized TRB producer publishes Enable Slot, Address Device, Evaluate Context, Configure Endpoint, and Disable Slot commands with cycle-state wrap, rings doorbell zero, matches completion pointers and slot identities, links the zeroed Device Context into DCBAA only after successful allocation, and clears the entry only after successful disable. The lifecycle then emits exact GET_DESCRIPTOR Setup, Data, and Status Stage TRBs, rings the slot endpoint-zero doorbell, accepts only a successful Status Stage Transfer Event with the expected pointer, slot, endpoint, zero residual, and no Event Data flag, validates the eight-byte device-descriptor prefix, and uses Evaluate Context before the next transfer when a full-speed device reports a larger endpoint-zero packet size. A second exact transfer retrieves the complete 18-byte descriptor, validates BCD encoding, the class/subclass relationship, USB generation, evaluated packet size, and nonzero configuration count, and retains the parsed identity until disconnect. The lifecycle then reads the first configuration header and exact reported tree up to the full 16-bit USB length limit; every Data Stage requests short-packet events, while a streaming parser validates framing, attributes, interface and endpoint counts, endpoint addresses, and required SuperSpeed companions without a configuration-sized kernel-stack copy.
