A successful exact no-data SET_CONFIGURATION transfer is followed by an exact host-to-device class/interface SET_PROTOCOL(Boot) request whose interface index comes from the selected descriptor; both endpoint-zero Status Stage completions must match before Configure Endpoint publishes A0 plus only the selected interrupt-IN DCI, a disabled endpoint state, CErr 3, DCS 1, and its dedicated ring. The port becomes configured only after the matching command completion, and no interrupt TD is posted before all three transitions succeed. The native idle loop keeps one-shot timer delivery armed while reset, command, or control-transfer progress is pending, and unsupported speeds, malformed descriptors, mismatched completions, timeout, malformed lifecycle, or DMA-fault paths quiesce the controller and revoke bus mastering.

The real xHCI hotplug path now retains an old slot, endpoint contexts, and exact transfer ownership while suppressing disconnected input. It stops running endpoint-zero and keyboard endpoints, validates a ring-owned forced stopped Transfer Event before each matching Stop Endpoint completion, and disables the slot before releasing DCBAA ownership or enumerating a replacement. An exact owned USB Transaction Error also requires live detachment or connection-change evidence before retirement; Halted endpoints use Reset Endpoint with transfer state preserved, and an exact successful command plus the Stopped context state is required before releasing their transfers. A combined removal and insertion notification retires the old lifetime even when the port is already connected again. Endpoint transitions follow authenticated events instead of potentially stale context snapshots; successful Stop and Reset completions still require a Stopped context. A matching Stop Context State Error can wait only for its exact owned transaction-error event under the original command and retirement deadlines. Already queued successful completions drain without parsing descriptors or publishing reports; report reservations release exactly once and preserve another port's control transfer. Repeated disconnect/reconnect notifications cannot extend the six-second retirement deadline, and each command retains its one-second timeout. Host tests drive the real lifecycle handlers and DMA event-ring consumer with owned memory and modeled MMIO, covering pending enumeration, delayed and combined notifications, transfer errors before port notifications, endpoint stop/reset ordering, reconnect reset, stale events, and report-capacity recovery. Physical controller hotplug and keyboard input remain unverified.

Production driver attachment requires explicitly detected, non-synthetic, target-grade device inventory before minting authority or attaching data planes. Input inventory and permission review are xHCI-only: PCI class and live capability validation publish only the USB controller, input-device authority waits for keyboard enumeration plus hardware event-ring evidence, and the kernel PS/2 scancode driver, IRQ1 handler, fallback poller, and PS/2 inventory source are absent; hosted modeled boots still seed explicit I225-LM/NVMe/xHCI inventory records.

Production runtime scheduling now requires invariant-TSC x2APIC deadline interrupts with an architectural TSC frequency. Logical time catches up directly from the invariant counter after delayed interrupts, scheduler wakeups use phase-aligned one-shot deadlines, and the native idle loop disarms its deadline when no task is runnable. The calibrated periodic x2APIC countdown path is isolated behind the explicit QEMU-only software CPU fallback that production media forbids. The QEMU harness selects KVM with the host CPU when a Linux runner exposes it and otherwise uses an x2APIC-capable software CPU with a pinned architectural TSC rate. Both legacy PICs are fully masked, PIT programming and IRQ stubs are absent, and production readiness rejects their restoration.

The production CPU baseline requires PGE, PCID, INVPCID, architectural SYSCALL/SYSRET, and RDPID. Every boot requires RDPID, including explicit software-emulator fallback boots. BSP/AP native entry binding publishes and verifies a bounded logical CPU number in IA32_TSC_AUX before entry or allocator access. Scheduler ownership, private syscall state and allocator cache lookup use that range-checked signature independently of userspace GS selectors or bases, without a privileged MSR read on the lookup path. Boot enables CR4.PGE and CR4.PCIDE before paging handoff, marks every shared supervisor-only kernel leaf global, assigns one bounded nonzero identifier to each userspace address space, samples the immutable process-context mode once during paging initialization, precomputes each validated CR3 switch value, preserves translations across typed user and kernel transitions, skips redundant switches, and invalidates each context before identifier reuse; user mappings remain non-global and the generic flush-on-every-switch API is absent. Software-emulator boots may use the typed flushing path only when the QEMU-only boot configuration supplies its explicit CPU fallback flag, which the production boot configuration forbids. Native userspace entry uses SCE, STAR/LSTAR/FMASK, a GS-based kernel-stack switch, RDI/RSI/RDX request arguments, RAX/RDX/R10 results, and SYSRET; the former user-callable software-interrupt syscall and yield gates are absent. Booted address-space round-trip and 64,000-operation syscall entry benchmarks measure both transition paths directly through the KVM-first validation harness with the calibrated software-emulator fallback. The benchmark keeps its installed diagnostic ELF symbolized but boots a separately linked debug-stripped derivative so UEFI firmware and GRUB do not parse non-loadable debug sections.

A composed kernel hardware-proof module now gates NUC markers on real SKU evidence, Multiboot memory-map handoff, GOP hardware framebuffer scanout proof evidence, mapped and checksum-validated ACPI MADT/FADT/MCFG/DMAR discovery, completed VT-d DMA and interrupt translation for independent NVMe, I225, and xHCI requesters, an observed requester/address/direction-matched blocked NVMe DMA write, APIC hardware LAPIC timer proof evidence, xHCI hardware event-ring input proof evidence, NVMe hardware-DMA write/read proof evidence, I225 hardware descriptor-ring packet proof evidence, hardware power-transition suspend/resume proof counts, hardware reboot-persistence crash-record proof counts, and hardware power-cycle update rollback proof counts.

The RNUC15CRSU7 proof bundle contract requires two distinct real-hardware single boots: production-serial.log binds the shipped production ISO/kernel to BOOT:ROLE:production, early SKU/Multiboot/ACPI facts, essential readiness, a structured clean error=none checkpoint, and native-ready; verification-serial.log binds the verification ISO/kernel to BOOT:ROLE:verification, native-ready, the exhaustive marker contract, and observation-before-PASS ordering.

Production readiness rejects QEMU-only or scalar-only evidence: a canonical capture statement binds a fresh nonce, stable device identity, repo IDs, both log hashes, both ISO/kernel pairs, both marker contracts, every sidecar, a canonical manifest of individually hashed cycle logs, and two role quote/signature pairs; an externally pinned verifier must return the exact statement-digest and nonce assertion.

Trusted native PIN submission now schedules a same-CPU cooperative worker on a lazy 128 KiB guarded supervisor-only NX stack. Entry erases its PIN before the first step; TPM command boundaries and hardware waits yield without held locks. Cancellation leaves the prompt locked, finishes active commands to identify created handles, permits only cleanup flushes afterward, and erases the private PIN and entire stack at completion. Actual elapsed time, current key policy and the exact pinned catalog are checked before exposing success. Teardown drains pending cancellation before borrowed stores can be released. Host tests cover suspended command borrows, late replies, time rollback, expiry, floating-point control preservation and nested-worker refusal. QEMU uses the native input/render/deadline path, dispatches a userspace task while the worker is suspended, checks stack permissions, cancels both before and after catalog restore, verifies cleanup and reopens successfully. Production now retains an identity owner through boot discovery, setup and sign-in; physical trusted input and TPM validation, biometric verification and userspace identity dispatch remain open.

Identity-session enrollment now requires an independently pinned persistent TPM storage-parent handle and Name. Opening checks the exact ECC template, public Name and qualified Name, then proves private-key possession using a salted HMAC session with encrypted ReadPublic output. Ordinary unlock never creates a primary or requests owner authorization. Explicit provisioning authenticates existing parents before reconciling persistence and never evicts them; owner authorization changes encrypt the new value and authenticate the reply with it. NV definition borrows owner authorization without retaining it. Disposable ownership boot proofs cover an interrupted persistence reply, protected-owner enrollment, damaged parent and authorization-change replies, restart unlock and replacement-TPM refusal. Administrator recovery custody, userspace identity dispatch and physical TPM validation remain open.

Canonical public identity enrollment now binds owner, device, PIN capsule, persistent TPM parent, catalog, NV index and key IDs to an independent digest. A fixed 176-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 recovery package authenticates that full binding and encrypts separate random owner, lockout and vault authorizations under an independently retained random 256-bit recovery key. It is committed before administrator changes; no PIN-derived recovery key or plaintext administrator record is supported. Explicit recovery validates the package before hardware access, authenticates the original parent before resetting DA lockout, restores the authenticated catalog and device keys, and emits recovery-key unlock proofs. Lock erases the verification method and revokes all leases and replay authority. Host tests corrupt every record/package byte, reject truncation and wrong binding/key/entropy, erase failed outputs, and refuse replacement TPMs without provisioning. The ownership reboot proof reloads random administrator secrets from disk ciphertext, exhausts eight PIN guesses, rejects invalid recovery before TPM commands, and tests failed anchor authentication, entropy failure, durable assertion counters, stale proofs and expiry. Trusted authentication now accepts PIN or recovery through the same exclusive keyboard router, masked compositor view and guarded cooperative worker. Ctrl+R selects recovery only when the owner attaches a recovery package. A 56-character base32 code represents the random key plus a domain-separated 24-bit typo checksum; grouped lowercase input is normalized privately, while the decoder requires a canonical compact code. Mode switches erase partial input, discard remaining events in the same report, drain queued reports and wait for fresh neutral input. Recovery decodes to the existing private 32-byte worker buffer; malformed codes allocate no worker and issue no TPM commands, and wrong keys fail package authentication before hardware. The ownership reboot proof types grouped codes through modeled HID, verifies masking and exclusive routing, dispatches userspace during TPM waits, checks protected worker pages, cancellation before and after catalog restore, erasure, recovery-method proofs, lock/reopen and expiry. Both methods recheck actual time and current policy before completion. The longer recovery proof exposed partial scheduler credit stranding a compositor between reading Open and sending its decision. New event activations now replenish to at least the configured task budget; duplicate wakes of an already-ready task add no credit, and explicit zero or partial refills remain exact. Host tests cover a two-dispatch interaction after a partly spent activation and repeated wakes, and the ownership boot continues through document-launch verification. Recovery-key custody, physical TPM persistence, userspace identity dispatch and lost-TPM backup remain open.

A serialized first-user provisioning service generates hardware-sealed catalog, root and device signing keys plus independent random owner, lockout and vault authorizations. It stages a signed catalog and canonical recovery bundle without permanent TPM changes. The caller independently retains the exact bundle pin and random recovery key before explicit commit, which authenticates both objects and completes one durable storage barrier before parent persistence, hierarchy authorization changes or NV enrollment. Salted audit-session GetCapability authenticates hierarchy-state flags, so an explicit retry uses the retained new authorization when a successful change lost its response; it never falls back to guessing the old value. The thirteen-boot ownership proof invokes this service, loses accepted replies at persistence, owner authorization, lockout authorization, lockout parameters, catalog NV definition and first write, and boot-pin definition, first write and persistent locking, and recovers across a VM/TPM restart at each boundary. It rejects forged hierarchy state before administrator commands, completes an already written anchor without rewriting, and rejects a replacement TPM during setup and normal sign-in. A separate fixture credential then exercises durable PIN/recovery sessions; fixture custody keys and signers remain verification-only. Host tests cover every bundle byte, independent pin binding, invalid inputs, wrong recovery keys, failed durability before TPM access, and the shared catalog/companion crash boundary. Native first-user setup now confirms the PIN before generating secrets on a guarded cooperative worker under the shared TPM lease. It makes the encrypted candidate durable before displaying a four-line 128-character recovery record carrying both the independent bundle pin and random recovery key. The user must retain the record outside the device and re-enter it after the display is hidden before permanent TPM changes. Ctrl+R resumes interrupted setup through the same private keyboard path. Input stays exclusive through completion; cancellation drains borrowed commands and erases private buffers and the complete 128 KiB worker stack. In-place credential and device resets avoid large temporaries that exceeded that stack in Debug. Retrying cancelled preparation uses fresh object IDs to preserve any retained candidate. The ownership proof now enters setup through modeled HID and native rendering, reads the recovery record from display cells, models independent custody with verification-only encryption and signing keys, checks mismatch/cancellation before provisioning, dispatches userspace during TPM waits and re-enters the record across nine interrupted commits. Normal recovery accepts the same record and compares its independent pin before TPM access. Host tests cover full-record checksum, canonical framing, erasure, input bounds, timeouts, clock reversal, private routing and command-buffer lifetime. Provisioning bundle v3 also binds a separate boot NV index. Commit preflights conflicts before permanent mutations, then writes the 48-byte public bundle pin under owner authorization and permanently locks the index using WRITEDEFINE. Definition commits the exact pin and index before data publication; retries authenticate and compare existing bytes without rewriting or relocking. Boot discovery takes its candidate from TPM state independently of disk, verifies the bundle and enrolled parent, and requires a salted HMAC read of the complete locked index before exposing enrollment to PIN entry. Disk publication is rechecked after device waits. The local TPM transport and verified boot remain the device trust boundary. Missing, partial, changed or replaced TPM state fails without provisioning. Reboot proofs reject incomplete state, damaged disk metadata and a corrupted authenticated read, and verify zero owner commands, writes, locks or DA resets on ordinary loading. The saved external recovery record remains necessary for interrupted setup and recovery. Production now allocates a stable native identity owner after measured boot and before surface presentation. Asynchronous discovery starts without keyboard input and remains exclusive through failure or cancellation. Explicit retry reruns discovery; an independently saved record can resume setup after configuration binding checks before TPM changes. Completion reloads the pinned bundle, releases the setup stack and binds PIN/recovery sign-in through a neutral-report barrier. Native expiry revokes authority before userspace dispatch. Catalog and recovery-bundle publication reacquire storage heads after hardware signing waits; concurrent first publication and later updates fail without overwriting the intervening writer. Host collision tests exercise both catalog cases and companion publication. In-place backing initialization avoids large stack temporaries; reset and failed boot detach and drain entries before erasing and freeing private state. Ownership proofs use this same retained owner for setup, handoff, reboot discovery, sign-in, lock/reopen and cancellation during teardown; production smoke with no TPM requires the unavailable locked outcome before idle. No fixture signing seed enters production. The shipped account path adds about 240 KiB of production code/data, with a bounded 3500-symbol ReleaseFast budget and explicit exclusion of identity proof modules. Provisioning bundle v3 carries a compact policy signed by the sealed identity root. The independently pinned bundle binds the issuer and user before attachment; no self-authenticated policy or software fixture signer is accepted. The native session checks the enrolled maximum duration before PIN or recovery hardware access and authenticates hardware key custody before activation. The baseline caps private key leases and credential unlock age, requires hardware custody, local unlock and phishing resistance, and denies raw export. Runtime configuration may shorten the enrolled limit. Host tests reject every changed policy byte, foreign issuers and owners, invalid framing, excessive leases, software keys, raw export, password fallback and stale unlock. The ownership reboot proof verifies attachment, clamps a longer boot configuration, and rejects overlong sessions and corrupted policy without any TPM command before ordinary sign-in and lock/reopen. The baseline is immutable; old provisioning formats have no fallback. Userspace identity dispatch, policy updates and recovery-material custody remain open; this does not provide lost-TPM backup or physical persistence evidence.
production_gaps: The repo can now emit the shipped production kernel's early NUC identity/ACPI evidence and the verification kernel's exhaustive subsystem PASS and concrete hardware fact markers only when the corresponding facts are present, but neither required real RNUC15CRSU7 boot log has been captured.
Production and verification media now boot native unified EFI images with embedded kernel and options; neither has been proven on the selected NUC firmware.

ACPI 2 RSDP, XSDT, MADT, MCFG, DMAR, APIC timer interrupt proof modeling, FADT discovery, and suspend/resume proof modeling are wired into post-paging mapped proof capture. NVMe second-stage translation, deny-all interrupt remapping, register or queued invalidation, primary fault-record decoding, and controlled blocked-write proof are programmed and proof-gated on the selected target, but a fresh archived real-machine capture is still pending. NUC APIC timer marker recording rejects modeled-only LAPIC timer proof without hardware register/interrupt evidence, and NUC suspend/resume marker recording rejects modeled-only ACPI suspend proof without hardware power-transition evidence, but no real DMAR/enforcement capture, LAPIC timer interrupt run, PCIe ECAM inventory, or suspend/resume cycle has been captured on the target hardware.

The framebuffer descriptor validator is wired to Multiboot/GOP-style framebuffer handoff, native compositor presentation is proof-gated in the modeled framebuffer, and the kernel GOP marker now rejects modeled-only framebuffer samples without hardware GOP scanout evidence, but the native profile now maps the firmware framebuffer and renders compositor-owned surfaces through bounded damaged-cell updates, but real GOP ownership and rendering still need capture on HDMI/framebuffer output.

Crash record formatting and recovered-record persistence proof are tested, and NUC crash marker recording now rejects modeled-only persistence without hardware reboot-persistence evidence, but real crash records are not yet written before reboot or consumed by a recovery boot on the target hardware.

PCI target identification, a real NVMe MMIO/queue/PRP bootstrap path with remapped-MSI runtime completion waits, real firmware-link-dependent I225-LM queued transmit and remapped-MSI deferred receive paths, executable modeled NVMe completion proof cycles, and executable modeled I225 interrupt, PHY-link, and TX/RX packet proof cycles are tested; NUC storage marker recording rejects modeled-only NVMe completions without hardware-DMA evidence and NUC network marker recording rejects the modeled path without hardware TX/RX cycle evidence. Fresh real-machine capture of both interrupt-driven controllers, including the complete PHY-backed network proof, remains pending.

xHCI 1.1+ live capability-register reads, typed BAR validation, bounded extended-capability traversal, sparse Supported Protocol port mapping, default and explicit PSI speed validation, one-second OS/firmware ownership handoff, CNR gating, 16 ms halt enforcement, bounded controller and port reset, cycle-tracked Enable Slot, Address Device, Evaluate Context, Configure Endpoint, and Disable Slot command submission, disconnect reuse, DCBAA completion ordering, slot-private endpoint-zero and interrupt-IN rings, direction-isolated report buffers, Input/Slot/endpoint context encoding, exact first and full device-descriptor control-transfer encoding and completion validation, full-speed packet-size adjustment, complete descriptor parsing and identity retention, short-packet-contained first-configuration retrieval, full-length streaming tree validation, default-alternate boot-keyboard selection, exact Set Configuration and interface-scoped Set Protocol (Boot) transfer completion, real interrupt-IN endpoint configuration, real report-TD posting and recycling, hardware Transfer Event validation, bounded report publication with controller backpressure, stale-ring invalidation, configured interrupt-transfer validation, modeled MMIO doorbell, context-memory, ERST, and event-ring proof, event-counted delivery, and boot-keyboard HID report handling are tested. The freestanding profile binds the real xHCI report queue and proof to one compositor-owned router. That router validates topology and monotonic sequence state, maintains independent transition decoders for four keyboards, uses a shared 32-event pool with a 16-event per-task ceiling plus counted overflow and stale-owner pruning, handles task switching centrally, routes modal input to the reviewer and ordinary input to the focused subject, keeps recovery input with the compositor, and wakes the selected userspace task. The v9 native ABI exposes semantic input descriptors through a task-targeted input_recv operation, streams endpoint payloads and optional transferred capabilities into prevalidated caller-owned outputs behind a 56-byte fixed response carrying a kernel-recorded sender endpoint, and defines a fixed 512-byte surface presentation copied through task-scoped authority into compositor-owned indexed storage. The presentation path validates active task-to-surface identity, canonical text and flags, monotonic revisions, idempotent retries, conflicting revisions, and bounded surface capacity; accepts initial state before a task view exists; prunes state for terminated tasks; and renders only the compositor's copy. Session routing mints receive and presentation authority only for eligible tasks, the kernel polls and presents through injected compositor receivers, and the 224-byte mailbox v7 publishes kernel-classified role and heartbeat metadata plus service, input, surface, state-revision, acknowledged-revision, failure-count, and status telemetry separately. UI-owning userspace tasks drain at most eight events per dispatch, fold them into one allocation-free state revision, submit one fixed snapshot, acknowledge only accepted revisions, and retain failed revisions for retry. An explicit yield disposition parks those tasks when their input queue is empty, keeps them runnable while a bounded drain may have more work, accounts event waits in scheduler telemetry, and relies on focused-router wakeups to requeue work without steady-state polling. Each UI process owns a fixed 512-byte text model with monotonic event rejection, bounded overflow, interaction hashing, text editing, focus, activation, recovery, and commit transitions. Notes, Viewer, Capture, Permission Review, and the compositor select distinct model roles, and the yield handoff exposes revisions for scheduler-side update telemetry. Production boot now provisions the compositor's task-scoped presentation right, drains startup work within a fixed budget, verifies that the userspace revision reached compositor-owned storage, checks mailbox acknowledgement and failure telemetry, renders the copied revision through the modeled framebuffer, and emits the surface-presentation marker only after that end-to-end proof. Boot service authorities begin at runtime tick zero rather than synthetic contract-order ticks, avoiding a startup clock-domain denial. Permission command editing consumes only routed events for its task while retaining a modeled controller for hosted verification. The shared decoder validates reserved, rollover, and duplicate-key state, emits only new key transitions, applies atomic queue backpressure, and translates Shift punctuation plus navigation, task-switch, recovery, activation, editing, and commit shortcuts. The shell stages bounded text edits and persists them only on Ctrl+Enter instead of writing storage for every keystroke. Service endpoints now have no implicit reply peer: replies explicitly name a connected client endpoint, preserve the request correlation id, and reject unrelated or stale generational endpoint handles without publishing a message or moving an attached capability. Native ABI v9 adds a distinct endpoint_close operation and right plus a peer_closed result. Closing an endpoint releases its unread moved grants, revokes all authority to that endpoint, returns its owner budget, and wakes surviving peers only after retirement. Connected peers retain queued replies and then observe terminal closure; closed connections cannot be rebound, while shared service ports remain available after an individual client closes. A single bounded scan identifies retired generational peers without comparing every surviving endpoint against every retired endpoint. Host syscall tests exercise permission failures, old-ABI rejection, parked-peer wakeup, final-reply drainage, terminal send/receive results, stale close requests, authority disposal, and parking after closure without spinning. Successful endpoint publication wakes the destination owner after any capability move, denied or full-queue sends do not wake tasks, duplicate messages coalesce into one ready-queue entry, and an owner-indexed pending-message check prevents parking over queued work. Kernel initialization now binds an exclusive synchronous runtime retirement hook, and deinitialization compares and unbinds its owner before the kernel storage is released. All runtime termination paths, including lifecycle policy requests and userspace exception containment, retire task-scoped grants, owned endpoint targets, owned shared-memory targets, and peer mappings before clearing task attachments. This removes the separate capability snapshot from the syscall termination path and adds one bounded 24-byte sink to the runtime. Host tests cover direct termination, surviving peer resources, hook exclusivity, callback ordering, and exactly-once retirement. The booted general-protection fault proof now provisions real kernel-owned endpoint and shared-memory resources and requires their grants, objects, and mappings to disappear after exception containment. Termination releases unread moved grants before freeing endpoint queues, and failed receive attachment releases a consumed move while preserving sender-owned copies. Regression tests cover receiver grant quotas, global grant exhaustion, expiry, and queue wraparound without reclaiming already-consumed entries. Endpoint and shared-memory creation now unwind unpublished objects when ownership grants fail, preserving existing objects and owner quotas; shared-memory rollback also restores its tail frame reservation. Single capability grants reserve a capability slot before creating target metadata, so repeated failed creations cannot exhaust target-generation entries. Host regressions exercise repeated per-task and global quota failures and successful retry after capacity is released. Removing a target's last grant now reclaims its target-generation record and invalidates the recent-target cache, avoiding a lifetime cap on object creation. Epochs remain live while any sibling grant exists, including revoked siblings; tests cover hundreds of unrelated target lifetimes, batch rollback, stale resolved handles, and fresh grants issued alongside revoked siblings. Userspace services explicitly close both temporary startup-check endpoints after the roundtrip completes, and unwind them on startup failure, returning their queues and grants instead of consuming lifetime endpoint capacity. Generic and service processes now request event waits when idle instead of remaining runnable for heartbeat updates; the production smoke test waits until all ready work drains and the boot loop disarms its scheduler tick. Both optimized production boots reached that idle marker. A QMP USB keyboard wake probe stopped at UnsupportedVersion for the available emulated controller; input wake after idle still needs validation on a controller meeting the xHCI 1.1+ baseline. The compositor ELF now browses authorized workspace documents in bounded pages and connects Open and Cancel to the Notes document-session opener, with cold-boot and reboot proofs; the production launch flow still needs durable identity and permission provisioning; a bounded text desktop now writes the firmware framebuffer through a supervisor-only uncached mapping with damaged-cell updates, while physical monitor capture and accelerated GPU scanout remain open; NUC keyboard marker recording rejects modeled-only xHCI input without hardware event-ring evidence, and real hardware-owned device contexts and input reports have not been captured from the controller.

The shipped production image still needs a real-device clean native-ready capture; real suspend/resume, crash recovery, crash-record persistence, update rollback across physical power cycles, compositor framebuffer capture, and booted verification-workload marker capture need the separate verification image and logs; NUC update rollback marker recording now rejects modeled-only selector rollback without hardware power-cycle evidence.

tracks.title: Userspace launch and service image provenance
current_evidence: The build generates a userspace image archive and production artifact manifest for freestanding boot profiles.
Launch provenance, component ABI metadata, signed bundle state, and syscall-dispatched task creation are enforced in native modules.

Task-create syscalls snapshot all four bounded launch strings and the executable image descriptor into kernel scratch before dispatch. Native ABI 19 validates and prepares fixed request and response storage before mutation, checks the full declared output span, and performs freestanding copies through owned physical page aliases. Host regressions preserve endpoint quota and grants, queued input, and wait disposition on invalid outputs; self-termination acknowledges solely through syscall status after retiring its address-space record.
Negative tests reject unsigned userspace launches and modeled runtime bypasses.
The production-readiness gate rejects unmarked syntheticUserspaceImage fixtures in critical launch and service test paths; existing synthetic fixtures are marked model-only.

The catalog registration path now uses an arena-backed image table with a bundle secondary index, rejects metadata-only executable registration, and rejects generated userspace artifacts when embedded ELF bytes are missing or malformed, when precomputed digests no longer match, or when generated ELF metadata and manifest state become stale.

Boot-registered userspace images now preload from the generated userspace archive on host and freestanding builds; the boot registry rejects missing or unregistered generated artifacts, and registered launch paths refuse metadata-only catalog records for all launch bundles.

Rendered-shell task launch now resolves executable metadata from the generated userspace image archive by bundle id and fails closed outside model-only tests when a configured bundle lacks a generated image.
Compositor task-view checkpoint tests now persist and restore app-linked windows for generated archive-backed app tasks instead of synthetic executable descriptors.
OS contract process-isolation checks now create contract tasks from generated userspace image fixtures instead of synthetic executable descriptors.
Host launch, service, syscall, storage, sync, and scheduler tests now use generated-image fixture readers for archive-backed executable descriptors in critical userspace paths.

The QEMU native smoke gate now requires generated userspace artifacts, scheduler binding, userspace exec/resume probes, service contract registration, service IPC connectivity, and driver restart markers before native-ready.
The service registry now rejects invalid bootstrap endpoints, zero binding identifiers, and unknown service connection flags before registering typed interfaces.

Typed service registration, discovery, and wire-message validation now require the one exact schema version; implicit minor-version compatibility is absent, and registry bindings retain only compact interface identifiers instead of duplicate contract pointers and version fields.

Component wire ABI v2 derives interfaces from globally unique operation and interface identifiers: every request header drops eight bytes of redundant version and flag metadata, service registration drops another eight bytes of repeated name/version state, connection requests and responses retain explicit zeroed padding, and ABI v1 messages fail closed.

The component schema enforces contiguous interface identifiers and resolves typed contracts by direct index; the service registry uses those same 31 exact slots instead of a 64-entry hash index and generic arena metadata, making binding-slot resolution constant-addressed and reducing resident registry state from 2,472 to 1,248 bytes. Adjacent default builds reduce the production boot payload by 8,192 bytes (15,335,424 to 15,327,232) and the verification payload by 4,096 bytes (20,357,120 to 20,353,024); paired ReleaseFast builds reduce the production payload by 4,096 bytes (6,225,920 to 6,221,824) while the verification payload remains 7,561,216 bytes.

Typed service registration and discovery accept only exact interface identifiers, eliminating manifest-name scans, repeated version validation, and the unsupported-name/version error branches from the registry hot path; declarations remain a schema and packaging concern before runtime binding. tracks.title: Live sync and private overlay transport
current_evidence: Sync state covers device graph enrollment, durable inbound/outbound frame queues, replay rejection, selective policy, per-object sharing, CRDT merge semantics, secret transfer markers, transactional database contracts, and explicit conflict review/resolution.

The two-node QEMU gate now runs ciphertext and replay rejection on the managed connection used for durable object transfer. It removes the former standalone channel proof, which discarded the final confirmation after local TX acceptance and could leave the other guest waiting. A bounded localhost relay deliberately drops the first two identical final confirmations and requires retransmission before the existing durable transfer, reopen, acknowledgement and owner-retirement assertions pass. Both sync and storage task suspension retire queued establishment state; stale handles remain rejected. The session manager no longer exposes unmanaged handshake attachment or handoff. Relay tests cover exact loss selection, stream fragmentation and coalescing, malformed lengths, bidirectional forwarding and socket shutdown.

Device graph enrollment, rotation and revocation validate the stored user-root signature, require the matching cryptographic root key regardless of signer label, and enforce device ownership. Existing roots cannot be reopened with a different key. Enrollment retries must preserve the current device key, label and platform binding; generation exhaustion and malformed root metadata fail before mutation. Host regressions cover forged and cross-user operations through both the graph and an authorized sync port, and the booted sync service proof rejects forged enrollment, rotation and revocation before normal replication. Operational root-pin provisioning remains open. The durable identity boundary now checkpoints sealed-key graph mutations and restores them under an independently supplied root pin.

SyncService now rebuilds resident workspace-policy, overlay, database-contract, conflict, and transport-frame path indexes from persisted state on startup, then services selective-policy, overlay, transactional-contract id, bundle, equivalence, conflict review, and latest-frame-by-path lookups through keyed indexes instead of scanning fixed persistent arrays.

Transport-frame path indexes now retain forward and backward links: latest-frame queries start at each queue tail and stop at the first collision-checked path match, durable arbitrary unlink updates neighboring links directly instead of scanning the bucket, and restart rebuilds sort live slots by frame id before restoring ordered indexes.

Replay-window enforcement now retains one collision-checked high-water link per active inbound workspace, source, and target scope, rebuilds those links from live frames on restart, and avoids repeated target-wide maximum scans; subtraction-based window comparisons remain defined at maximum frame identifiers.

Inbound duplicate detection now uses a collision-checked index over the complete workspace, source, target, and source-frame scope, keeping admission lookup bounded while enqueue, replay-window eviction, and restart reconstruction preserve exact durable membership.

The overlay relay service rejects unauthorized relay use, target changes, empty encrypted packets, malformed zero-tick/zero-task egress requests, and relay fallback re-checks revoked device trust before enqueueing failed native sends across both disconnected/congested and post-send network-failure paths.

Overlay session opens now return an in-process, read-only borrow of the authoritative service-owned record instead of copying three maximum-sized text buffers back through the service, authority-port, and SDK layers; the lifetime contract requires a stable Service or DevNode address, and closed-state visibility plus the slot-reuse boundary are regression-tested, while paired QEMU samples reduce the full open/probe/close flow by 4.1 to 5.0 percent with unchanged checksums.

Overlay session ids now encode their bounded slot and generation directly, replacing repeated hash lookups during probe, read, close, and reuse while invalidating retired ids before a slot is overwritten; closed records remain readable until reuse, stale probe and close calls fail, the session arena shrinks from 2,160 to 1,968 bytes, the separate 8-byte id cursor is gone, and three consecutive ReleaseFast software-emulator samples reduce the full flow from 1,329.87-1,345.62 to 1,059.12-1,065.25 cycles per operation, a 19.9-21.3 percent improvement with the expected handle-derived checksum.

Native sync transport ABI host tests now bind captured frames to source and target task ids, require nonce/tag authentication and a keyed MAC over the complete v4 wire header, reject zero or malformed frame headers, reject non-device or same-device endpoints, enforce packet/session metadata before encoding, reject invalid task ids before endpoint allocation, preflight packet-capture capacity and the 96-byte native endpoint/frame payload ceiling before endpoint or driver side effects, and fail closed on mutated encrypted packet metadata during decrypt.

The sync service no longer exposes its direct in-process Relay send path: end-to-end host tests replicate document, media, secret, and database payloads through NativeTransportService endpoint delivery and active-driver transmit first, use the booted relay service only as fallback, chunk payloads at the native transport ceiling, and prove object-scoped grants skip private entries while offline conflicts stay reviewable.

Sync, service-identity and discovery packet encryption now use the pinned XChaCha20-Poly1305 implementation with CSPRNG-generated 256-bit secrets, HKDF context binding and fresh random 192-bit nonces. Native sync ABI v4 authenticates its full header, including task routing and sequence, with a separately derived HMAC-SHA256 key. Authenticated decoding and decryption are distinct from diagnostic inspection, and failures erase bounded plaintext output. Debug tests cover a known cipher vector, every native-frame byte, wrong keys and contexts, fresh keys/nonces and failed entropy. Redundant device-kind and frame-policy copies are removed, preserving payload and memory ceilings while reducing packet/result records and relay backing.

Noise_XX_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256 now establishes directional traffic keys between independently booted nodes. Fresh X25519 static and ephemeral keys are separate from device Ed25519 signing keys; handshake certificates bind the static key to the pinned graph context. Enrollment/rotation signatures chain to an independently supplied user-root pin, and live key rotation/revocation invalidates channels. The channel is bounded to 544 bytes, authenticates all datagram routing/nonce fields, uses a 64-packet replay window updated only after successful decryption, erases failed plaintext and retired keys, and closes on send nonce exhaustion. Noise-c vectors cover all three handshake messages, the handshake hash and bidirectional transport; adversarial tests cover handshake/datagram corruption, truncation, forged certificates, stale sessions and trust changes. The two-node gate now requires peer authentication, ciphertext rejection and replay rejection on both guests, with timed cached-byte handshake retransmission that does not amplify queued duplicates, retryable transmit-ring backpressure and no preinstalled traffic secret.

Peer-channel initialization now requires a non-exportable sealed signing lease; raw device seeds are restricted to an explicitly named verification constructor that rejects production kernels. The shared 48-byte lease validates holder/task, owner, policy, expiry, revocation and ciphertext identity, and signs without exporting key material. Channel reads, writes and handshake steps recheck the lease and erase traffic keys and rejected output when it expires or is revoked. The channel keeps its existing 544-byte ceiling by reading the remote public key from the already checked graph instead of retaining a duplicate. Root creation, device enrollment, rotation and revocation have sealed-key entry points with the same signature and ownership checks. Host tests cover denied policies, expired/revoked leases, key/holder changes, wrong root keys and generation changes. The two-node object proof now uses the sealed channel and storage signing APIs through explicit software sealing fixtures; a separate TPM gate establishes and retires a channel using the generated device key on cold boot and the catalog-restored key after a full reboot. The TPM gate now generates the root and both device keys, commits their graph through the durable identity service, and restores the graph without reenrollment before authenticating after reboot. Separate authenticated TPM NV records now supply both catalog and graph pins independently of the native disk; the emulator proof uses public verification-only authorization. Operational root-pin and authorization provisioning and runtime peer discovery remain open.

Vault catalog v5 now commits one owner's canonical device graph with sealed keys and credential counters in one signed checkpoint. It preserves enrollment, rotation, revocation and platform-binding fields, rebuilds indexes, and restores no leases. A separate root pin is required for nonempty enrollment; signatures for the root and every trusted or revoked record are checked before any keys are unsealed. Graph publication waits for the entire key and credential restore, and wrong pins, forged inner records, duplicate devices, truncated data and failed unseals leave all destination stores empty. Local graph mutations require their private signing keys from the checkpointed vault, withhold success until the durable barrier, and block further mutations or graph access after failed checkpoints. Public enrollment approval accepts a remote device proof without holding that remote private key. Crash tests at both barriers recover the old graph and keys or the retried new snapshot together. Root generation and signed generation floors now have authenticated TPM NV storage, while production provisioning, physical persistence validation and interrupted first-enrollment recovery remain open; the existing sync-state workspace is not a substitute for this authenticated restore boundary.

A bounded object receiver accepts only authenticated peer-channel ciphertext, binds every operation to a locally selected object capability, workspace, peer and sync service, and rechecks writable path-scoped network shares and selective policy before staging. Its 240-byte coordination ceiling excludes caller-owned bounded scratch; 181-byte chunks require no network-driven allocation. Transfers bind to the Noise session, expire and erase staging, reject conflicting retries and concurrent local edits, sign replacements through a storage-service sealed signing lease, and acknowledge only a durable object-plus-workspace checkpoint. Failed write/barrier retries retain one pending version, while a fresh session recognizes already committed content after a lost receipt. Host tests cover capability/share/device/service revocation, wrong scopes, expiry, corruption, ordering, session replacement, conflicts and both power-loss barriers. The two-guest proof sends 1,024 freshly generated source bytes over encrypted chunks to a separately authorized target object, reloads the target storage service from its own disk before replying, and requires both target-reopen and source-receipt markers. Verification uses explicit fixture signers. Collections, event streams and secret objects are rejected by the byte-replacement protocol.

The runtime now admits up to four locally authorized established sealed peer channels into a 40-byte session table. Each caller-owned session is bounded to 672 bytes, holds one incoming and one outgoing ciphertext frame, accepts at most eight frames per 10 ms tick, and expires within 30 seconds. Round-robin dispatch performs at most two receive, encode or send operations per visit. Unknown routes are rejected before cryptography or allocation, and protocol-selective dequeue preserves unrelated receive order. Backpressured replies reuse sealed ciphertext and nonces after a 20 ms deadline; authority, graph trust and both signing leases are checked before every retry. Task suspension, termination, lost network devices, expiry and revoked authority retire channels and erase staging. Idle service work uses phase-aligned one-shot TSC deadlines. Host tests cover floods, revocation, durable retries, cached ciphertext and receive-slot reuse. The two-node gate transfers through this dispatcher, reloads the target object before its receipt, and suspends the sync task to prove admission cleanup. Operational peer provisioning remains separate work; bounded handshake admission is now implemented below.

The runtime now admits up to four locally registered Noise handshakes with sealed signing leases and sync-service capability authority. No packet can create a slot, select a pin or allocate cryptographic state. Deferred receive now uses a free-slot bitmap and compact ordering indexes, so an unread unrelated packet cannot strand emptied slots. While peer traffic is reserved, eight of the unchanged 32 packet slots serve that protocol and 24 serve other traffic; full or stalled consumers cannot consume the other class's capacity. Reservation keeps the oldest packets in each class and drops excess arrivals with existing counters. The 48,064-byte packet backing and zero-overflow-scratch ceiling are unchanged. A reproduced host regression covers more than three capacity turnovers behind a stalled generic consumer, and saturation tests preserve both classes' FIFO order. Each caller-owned handshake is bounded to 856 bytes and three 256-byte packet buffers, with eight accepted frames per tick and a ten-second maximum lifetime. Handshakes and object traffic alternate priority within the same two-operation dispatch budget. The dispatcher handles all three Noise flights and encrypted confirmation, caches exact retransmission bytes across loss and backpressure, ignores queued duplicates without immediate replies, and rechecks service authority, signer leases and graph trust before every operation or retry. Task suspension, lost devices, failed handshakes and expiry erase pending state. Successful handoff preserves the final confirmation ciphertext for application retries until remote application data proves delivery. Host tests drop each of the five flights, inject duplicate bursts, fill the slot table, test round-robin dispatch and reject invalid or revoked admission and handoff authority. Both QEMU guests establish a channel through this runtime table and prove pending-handshake retirement on sync-task suspension. The separate durable object proof now opens a service-owned connection with automatic handoff. The proof still rejects modified remote ciphertext and replay. Peer identities, pins and addresses are explicitly supplied; service-owned connection state is implemented below, while operational discovery and provisioning remain open.

A read-authorized runtime sender now drives offers, begins, storage-backed chunks, commit requests and durable receipts through the same four-slot peer table. Its 288-byte coordination ceiling adds no object-sized plaintext snapshot or retained storage pointers; each bounded cursor walk copies at most 181 requested bytes across storage pages. Admission pins the source version, blob address and channel, and every read or cached send rechecks the peer read capability, network share, selective policy, live service authority and sealed channel lease. An authenticated offer pins the destination once, and the serialized channel nonce supplies a nonreused request identifier. Receipts cannot acknowledge unsent ranges or claim durable success before a sent commit. Driver backpressure preserves exact ciphertext and nonce; an accepted request with a lost reply is resealed at its retry deadline so the receiver replay filter admits the idempotent retry. Host tests lose offers, begins, chunks, commits, progress and final receipts, cross a storage page, reject invalid receipts and retargeting, cancel queued egress after revocation or source edits, and retry failed durable barriers without adding a version. Both independent QEMU guests now run all object protocol traffic through runtime sessions; the source reads its persisted object and the target reopens durable bytes before its receipt. Both sides prove retirement on task suspension. The 672-byte session ceiling, 40-byte table and shared two-operation handshake/object dispatch budget are unchanged.

The session manager now owns up to four peer connections behind generation-checked handles in a 72-byte table. Each authorized local open allocates at most 2,048 bytes of coordination state and only the explicitly bounded receive limit; senders allocate no staging buffer. No packet allocates or reopens a connection. The owner retains stable channel, handshake and transfer state, revalidates source version and authority at handoff, preserves the final confirmation for loss recovery, and counts promotion against the existing two-operation dispatch budget. Revoked authority, failed authentication, expiry, task retirement and explicit release detach protocol pointers before scrubbing and freeing the owner and receive bytes. Generations survive manager reset and exhausted generations are retired instead of wrapping. Host tests transfer across storage pages while losing final confirmation or first application messages, reject stale handles and duplicate peers, fill all four slots, deny invalid local bindings and oversized receive limits, reject source edits or revocation before handoff, and preserve a separately admitted session when handoff fails. Both QEMU guests now transfer through manager-owned handles, require automatic promotion, suspend storage during pending establishment to prove owner reclamation and stale-handle rejection, then prove sync-task retirement after durable completion. The separate channel tampering and replay proof remains verification-only. Caller-provisioned service stores, pins, keys, peer addresses and object grants still outlive their connections; this runtime owner does not supply operational enrollment, discovery or reboot recovery.

Public device enrollment now exchanges bounded proof-of-possession and owner-consent messages, binding the device identity, label, overlay and independently supplied root pin. Root approval checkpoints the signed public record without a remote key lease. Root-signed graph publications cover all serialized metadata through a domain-separated digest, and import binds the local record to a private key in the receiving vault. Known membership, key generations, revocations and platform bindings cannot be rolled back; duplicate approvals and imports do not write another version. Host tests use separate vaults and disks, authenticate channels after both crash and reopen, corrupt every wire byte, reject truncation, wrong pins, changed consent, foreign keys, capacity overflow and same-generation rewrites, and inject both storage-barrier failures. The TPM guest now keeps its two device keys in separate vaults and catalogs, exchanges the public messages, and restores both catalogs with fresh leases before authenticating after reboot. Both vaults use the same guest TPM; independent hardware enrollment, user approval, transport, trusted pin provisioning and external rollback floors remain open.

Public device-key rotation now carries a bounded 306-byte request with the expected generation, prior key, successor proof and owner-root pin, signed by the current device key. Preparation requires both sealed-key leases in the device vault and checkpoints the replacement before releasing the request. Root approval verifies continuity against the current authenticated record, commits the new generation and makes matching retries idempotent. Import checks replacement-key custody and preserves rollback barriers; old channels retire through their existing graph checks. Host tests exercise every wire byte, framing, foreign or revoked leases, stale and competing rotations, generation exhaustion, platform-binding downgrade denial, and crash/retry at both barriers in preparation, approval and import. Failures after request publication retain a recoverable successor; failed preparation can safely generate another key. Recovery tests finish the rotation and authenticate after reopening separate disks. The TPM gate rotates the independently held remote key twice, retires its predecessors, reuses a slot with a new ID and restores the current key and separate catalog signer after reboot. Root approval certificates bind the exact predecessor consent and successor proof; a valid substitute consent cannot authorize deletion or pass graph authentication. Durable retirement requires the approved successor in the same vault, protects catalog signers, credential references, owner roots and trusted device keys, and checks policy and audit before removing all old leases and the current record. Catalog v4 persists slot generations and rejects forgotten tombstones, resurrected IDs and changed sealed bindings. Host tests cover 20 rotations across repeated restarts, stale IDs and handles, exhausted generations, protected references and both durability barriers with explicit retries. Existing store, service and graph memory ceilings are unchanged. Historical encrypted checkpoint versions remain retained, so secure erasure, lost-key recovery, user approval, transport, trusted pins and independent rollback floors remain open.

The two-node QEMU gate boots separate native nodes and native-store images with non-transitional VirtIO PCI networking. Its bounded 32-entry split queues require VERSION_1, ACCESS_PLATFORM and MAC; 136 KiB of pinned DMA has separate ring, receive-write and transmit-read windows. Exact firmware requester scopes, cache-maintained VT-d tables where required, a blocked DMA write probe and remapped MSI-X precede device activation. Both guests must receive encrypted native frames and observe a network interrupt, and the harness saves per-node wire captures. Device graph, policy, relay, revoked-device and persisted sync-service restart markers remain required on each node.

When an active network device is available, the booted sync scenario exercises encrypted native transport ABI frames through network_driver_task.sendActiveFrame, resolves the authenticated target device through a bounded peer-link directory, validates captured packets against transmitted frames, and rejects plaintext-on-wire evidence. The two-node gate requires packet-captured/frame-sent, malformed-packet rejection, reconnect, replay-window rejection, and congestion-backpressure markers. Reaching native-ready alone does not prove these checks ran.

NativeTransportService now has a production fail-closed mode that refuses endpoint delivery, packet capture, and active-driver transmit until a real Intel I225 proof with ring ownership, PHY link, tail-register writes, interrupts, MAC evidence, and the first-target network frame cycle count is attached.

TransportSession now records an explicit trust posture: relay/local-lab sessions remain local_lab_only, pinned service-identity sessions become production_attested only when verified remote attestation includes request-bound verifier metadata, and session key derivation binds the posture so lab and production sessions cannot share the same crypto context silently.

Network policy and transport session posture now require verified remote-attestation evidence with a bound verifier request digest and bound attestation verifier metadata digest before treating a pinned connection as production-attested; loose attested=true claims and root-pinned attestations without verifier metadata remain local-lab or denied for production policies.

Connection authorization now resolves each indexed network policy once and evaluates each scoped target comparison once before applying attestation pins, cutting the gated authorization benchmark roughly in half while preserving fail-closed destination and identity checks.

Network policies are append-only and bounded, so immutable sequential policy ids now address canonical dense slots directly while the remaining multimap is reserved for request deduplication; persisted rebuilds reject id-to-slot mismatches, the directory shrinks from 4,848 to 4,352 bytes, and three consecutive ReleaseFast software-emulator samples measure connection authorization at 71.18-73.21 cycles per operation and the full overlay session flow at 1,329.87-1,345.62 with unchanged checksums.

NativeTransportService now exposes a typed verified service-identity open path that consumes the attestation response/request, measured boot record, trusted root, and policy-pinned attestation verifier metadata digest directly; the production regression uses that path and proves a response for the wrong service identity or selected device cannot open a production session. Both the transport harness and native network stack compare the signed device identity with the selected peer before granting connection authority or sending packets.

The native network-driver service-identity path now carries verified-attestation state, the verifier request digest, and the request-bound attestation verifier metadata digest through connection creation, key derivation, frame metadata, and brokered transmit rechecks, with regression coverage proving brokered sends keep the same verified evidence instead of downgrading to loose attested flags.

The booted sync service-path proof now provisions its network identity root through the production external-provider boundary, requires a request-bound verifier metadata digest, and persists that digest into the service-identity network policy.

NativeTransportService can now require production-attested sessions before endpoint delivery, object-share encryption, packet capture, relay fallback, or active-driver transmit; the regression gate proves local-lab relay sessions stay blocked even after I225 hardware proof while pinned attested service-identity sessions can transmit.

The rendered production journey now surfaces the object-scoped trusted-overlay share grant and drives a real offline document conflict through sync conflict review/resolution, so object sharing and conflict handling are user-visible daily-driver evidence rather than backend-only sync assertions.

Sync checkpoints prepare immutable records under a bounded storage batch and publish the complete managed workspace directory in one generation, preserving unrelated entries. Allocation failures keep the previous directory intact; retries reconcile actual immutable object heads and reuse matching records. Required disk checkpoint failures and deferred outer batches withhold success. Retry state lives in existing resident padding and survives service reinitialization; fresh residents loaded from unflushed RAM also retain pending status. Duplicate and unchanged public operations retry the failed barrier, including the first registered or imported database contract. Host regressions cover full frame-queue rollover, late allocation failure, barrier failure with crash reload, service restart, and outer-batch deferral. Production service ownership and sealed checkpoint signing remain open.
production_gaps: The modern VirtIO two-node gate authenticates Noise channels and durably transfers a capability-authorized object between independent disks using explicitly provisioned fixture identities and peer MACs. Runtime dispatch of already established sealed channels is bounded and task-scoped. Operational device-key enrollment, root-pin provisioning, peer discovery and connection provisioning remain open. Bounded runtime admission now drives locally authorized handshakes as well as established object traffic, and the manager owns their state behind generation-checked handles with automatic handoff. The runtime sender and receiver support scoped byte replacement with live read/write authority and version-conflict rejection; continuous convergence, offline conflict resolution, typed collection/event-stream/secret operations and restart of a network transfer across full guest reboots remain open. Existing in-process replication still accesses both stores directly and is not evidence for remote object admission.
Real-hardware evidence still needs to capture the same sync markers on the RNUC15CRSU7 with the Intel I225-LM path active and packet counters tied to physical frames.

Remote device identity sessions are explicitly marked local-lab unless pinned verified attestation-response evidence with a verifier request digest and request-bound attestation verifier metadata digest is present, but production-grade remote trust still depends on the boot/attestation track wiring external providers to operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS roots.
graduation_criteria: Replace sync_transport_harness as the primary evidence with a native transport service that runs through endpoint syscalls and the network driver task.
Keep the two-node QEMU replication gate covering offline policy, device-to-device replication, relay fallback, revoked-device rejection, and persisted restart before release.
Bind production remote device sessions to operational attestation roots while keeping local-lab sessions explicitly labeled and rejectable by production-only callers.
next_actions: Connect bounded handshake and object admission to operational peer discovery and enrollment, then replace in-process replication with continuous independent-store convergence, offline conflict handling and full-reboot transfer recovery. Add explicit typed protocols for collections, event streams and secret objects. Connect the TPM NV-backed durable enrollment boundary to production authorization and first-enrollment provisioning, validate physical TPM persistence, and implement interrupted first-enrollment recovery before production use.
Replace external-provider software callback fixtures for production remote sessions with provisioned TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS-backed attestation roots.

current_evidence: The rendered-shell production journey is now scoped to one Notes app daily-driver path rather than a generic desktop expansion path.

The journey installs a signed native Notes package, starts its native component, opens a notes workspace and document, reviews the local object-access permission, grants an object-scoped collaborative share, syncs only after sharing, updates and rolls back the package, recovers shell/runtime state, removes the package, and revokes device and policy authority.
The share step writes a concrete trusted-overlay, object-scoped workspace grant and verifies the collaborator can read and write the shared note before sync proceeds.

tracks.title: Userspace driver data-plane depth
current_evidence: I225 and modern VirtIO TX queues now publish their earliest outstanding watchdog into the native idle wake schedule. Due expiry becomes pending device work without RX, completion interrupts, or another send; queue completions drain before timeout checks, and empty, contained, or inactive controllers remove their deadline. Host regressions invoke the production service handlers and native scheduler deadline bridge, including pre-deadline idle, timeout containment, early completion, and deadline saturation.

Driver registration checks signed bundles, device-class authority, DMA range metadata, restart generations, and a PCI/NVMe-only storage target whose bus mastering is confined to brokered staging, queue, and bounce-buffer windows.

I225 interrupt-storm accounting now observes TX descriptors reclaimed outside interrupt service and RX completions polled before delayed MSI delivery, including dropped packets. Actual descriptor progress resets the empty-interrupt streak without weakening the eight-consecutive-empty limit or oldest-TX timeout. Hosted regressions exercise the production reaper and completion observer through 128 completion/interrupt interleavings, ring wrap, unfinished descriptors and true no-progress containment; physical MSI timing remains part of the hardware capture gap.

The device broker now indexes controller slots and programmed DMA domains by device using arena/index-backed tables; unconfined bus mastering is rejected, and bus mastering is accepted only as a brokered-buffer program whose declared windows enumerate the exact queue or bounce frames the real NVMe engine may touch.

The device broker is PCI-only: hosted ATA state and legacy bootstrap modules are absent from every build, native ABI v9 exposes device description, MMIO discovery, bounded endpoint I/O with explicit service reply routing, and bounded surface presentation without port-I/O opcodes, and the device descriptor is compacted from 32 bytes to 16 bytes. Endpoint syscalls validate bounded user ranges and copy payloads through kernel-owned staging before queue publication; queued messages own their payload bytes and failed or oversized requests publish no message.

Storage driver tasks attach through a generation-scoped PCI controller session, validate their device authority at activation time, program the NVMe DMA envelope, and attach only capacity-checked NVMe publications to the freestanding volume.

The storage data-plane gate covers active-I/O restart, DMA fault containment, partial-transfer rejection, controller revocation, and explicit republish/rebind before post-restart I/O.

current_evidence: The kernel heap reclaims bounded cached spans across CPUs before declaring exhaustion. Per-CPU locks and exact recent publishers protect remote cache reuse and span recycling while the global lock serializes reclamation and coalescing. Host tests cover every cached class, live neighboring allocations, distinct-CPU concurrent reuse, and full metadata pressure without increasing the 100,370-byte allocator array budget; the allocator benchmark includes whole-arena cached-pressure reuse.
Scheduler decisions account for resource class, engine availability, thermal pressure, battery saver, privacy mode, CPU budget, memory bandwidth, and zero-copy shared memory.

Coalesced task wakes preserve the earliest queued deadline rather than extending it on every event; sustained foreground load with repeated background and batch wakes remains covered by bounded-service regressions. Failed accelerator claim reservation retains a queued waiter with no claim, and policy-denied online engines use the same eligibility-checked wait without a grant/requeue spin. Unrelated eligible work can pass those waiters; telemetry and request changes restore dispatch. Contradictory required-engine configurations are rejected before changing the prior request. Credential approval and verification worker wakes now use the session's common external-wake helper with the actual event time, with host timestamp coverage and a Ring3 approval-wake assertion.

Freestanding MMU mappings now use compact u16 intrusive links and a canonical per-object head/count instead of a second object multimap; mapping records retain only identity, domain, and virtual-address state, while descriptors derive immutable and generation fields from the arena-owned object on demand. Low-level mutation and descriptor methods are private so caller-owned object copies cannot corrupt list metadata, and regressions cover head/middle/tail unlinking, forced cross-object reuse of a freed slot, duplicate-versus-full errors, and revocation of a saturated mapping arena.
